#### Hotels in Santa Rosa, CA

Most hotels in Santa Rosa sit in one of two places: along the highway corridors on the edge of town, or downtown, where you can leave the car parked and walk to dinner. Downtown splits into Old Courthouse Square, the city's civic and dining center, and Historic Railroad Square a few blocks west around the restored train depot and the SMART station. Our hotels, Art House and Hotel E, are both on the Courthouse Square side, a short walk from each other, from the Museum of Sonoma County and from the restaurants and tasting rooms along 4th Street. From either one, the wineries of the Russian River Valley, Sonoma Valley and Dry Creek Valley are a short drive out, so you can spend the day in wine country and be back in town for dinner.

[See every downtown hotel in the directory →](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=hotels)

Our Mission

### About _Stay Santa Rosa_

Stay Santa Rosa's mission is to bring the best of Santa Rosa and the broader Sonoma County closer to you.

We believe that where you stay shapes how you experience a place. Created by Hotel E and Art House Santa Rosa, Stay Santa Rosa is a general guide to the city, pointing you to our two hotels, restaurants, tasting rooms and attractions rooted in downtown Santa Rosa and connected to the food, wine, culture, and landscapes that make Sonoma County one of the most remarkable corners of California.

Whether you're here for a weekend in the vineyards, an extended stay working remotely, a celebration with family, or simply a few days of good food and open roads, this guide is here to help you make the most of it.

### Planning a trip to _Santa Rosa_

Santa Rosa is the largest city in Sonoma County and the practical base for a wine country trip. It sits on Highway 101 about an hour north of the Golden Gate Bridge, with the Russian River Valley to the west, Sonoma Valley to the east, Dry Creek and Alexander Valley to the north, and the Sonoma Coast within an hour's drive. Unlike the small towns scattered around it, Santa Rosa has a walkable downtown, which means you can eat, taste and wander without getting back in the car every evening.

[Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) and [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) are two independent hotels a few minutes apart in that downtown core. Art House is contemporary, built around a rotating collection of work by local artists, with studios and suites for longer stays. Hotel E is a restored 1906 Beaux-Arts landmark on Old Courthouse Square with thirty-nine rooms and the Enology wine lounge on the ground floor. Both put Old Courthouse Square, Railroad Square and the 4th Street restaurant corridor within a short walk.

#### Where to eat

Downtown has become one of Northern California's more interesting restaurant corridors, from French bistro cooking to Neapolitan pizza, Puerto Rican plates and a proper steakhouse. Start with the [downtown dining guide](https://staysantarosa.com/dining), then open the [restaurant directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=dining) to see what is open right now.

#### Where to taste

Four appellations are within reach, and Santa Rosa has been called the microbrew capital of the country. The [wine and beer guide](https://staysantarosa.com/wine-country) covers the estates worth the drive, and the [winery and brewery directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=wine) lists tasting rooms and taprooms with current hours.

#### What to do

The Charles M. Schulz Museum, Luther Burbank's home and gardens, the Museum of Sonoma County, redwood groves, state parks and the coast. The [attractions guide](https://staysantarosa.com/attractions) and the [attractions directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=attractions) cover a first visit and a fifth one.

#### When to come

Harvest runs from late summer into fall and is the busiest, most atmospheric time to visit. Spring brings mustard bloom and green hills, and winter is the quietest season for tasting rooms. Our [journal](https://staysantarosa.com/blog) has longer local guides for each.

### Getting here

Santa Rosa sits on Highway 101 in the middle of Sonoma County, north of San Francisco and inland from the coast. Charles M. Schulz Sonoma County Airport is a short drive north of downtown, and San Francisco and Oakland international airports are the usual alternatives. A car makes wine country far easier, though the downtown restaurants, tasting rooms and taprooms in our [restaurant directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=dining) and [winery and brewery directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=wine) are walkable from the downtown hotels.

### Planning your days

Start with the directory. It lists real places with current hours, ratings and directions taken from the business's own Google profile, so you can see what is open before you set out.

- [Restaurant directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=dining), twenty-nine places to eat in and around downtown.
- [Winery and brewery directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=wine), tasting rooms across four appellations plus the local taprooms.
- [Attractions directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=attractions), museums, gardens, parks and the coast.
- [The journal](https://staysantarosa.com/blog), longer guides written by people who live here.

### Press and partnerships

For press enquiries, photography requests, or working with one of the hotels on an event or group stay, contact the property directly and ask for the sales team; phone numbers and websites are listed in the [directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=hotels). For questions about Stay Santa Rosa itself, email [hello@staysantarosa.com](mailto:hello@staysantarosa.com).

# Where to Stay

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/hotels
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Where to Stay in Santa Rosa: downtown boutique hotels steps from Courthouse Square, with suites, kitchens, pet-friendly rooms and wine country nearby.

Downtown Santa Rosa · Sonoma County

## Where to Stay in Santa Rosa: _Downtown Boutique Hotels_

Stay downtown and Santa Rosa works on foot: Old Courthouse Square, Railroad Square and the 4th Street restaurants are a short walk, and wine country starts 20 minutes out.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. Where to Stay

Why stay downtown

### The best area to stay in Santa Rosa

Downtown is the one part of Santa Rosa where you can leave the car parked. Old Courthouse Square sits at the center, the 4th Street restaurant corridor runs east from it, and Historic Railroad Square, with the SMART train station, is a short walk west across the highway.

From here the Russian River Valley, Sonoma Valley and Dry Creek Valley wineries are each roughly 20 to 30 minutes by car, the redwoods at Armstrong Woods about 35 minutes, and the Sonoma Coast under an hour. It is the most practical base for a first visit to Sonoma County.

[See every hotel in the directory →](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=hotels)

Our boutique hotels

### Two downtown hotels, _two different stays_

Hotel E and Art House Santa Rosa are a few minutes apart in the downtown core. Hotel E is the historic landmark on the square; Art House is contemporary, with studios and suites built for longer stays.

Historic

#### Hotel E Santa Rosa

37 Old Courthouse Square

A restored 1906 Beaux-Arts landmark right on Old Courthouse Square, with 39 rooms, the Enology wine lounge on the ground floor, continental breakfast, valet parking and dog-friendly rooms.

[Explore Hotel E →](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e)

Studios & suites

#### Art House Santa Rosa

620 7th Street

A contemporary boutique hotel and living art gallery, with studios and suites that have full kitchens, free breakfast, indoor parking, EV charging, bike lending and pet-friendly rooms.

[Explore Art House →](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house)

Side by side

### Hotel E or Art House?

|  | Hotel E | Art House

| Style | Historic 1906 Beaux-Arts landmark | Contemporary, rotating local art

| Location | On Old Courthouse Square | 7th Street, a short walk from the square

| Rooms | 39 rooms, king and queen | Studios and suites

| Kitchens | No | Yes, in studios and suites

| Breakfast | Continental breakfast | Free breakfast

| Parking | Valet | Indoor parking, EV charging

| Pets | Dog-friendly | Pet-friendly

| Best for | Wine weekends, couples, a night on the square | Extended stays, families, working remotely

Plan by trip

### Which hotel fits your trip

#### A wine country weekend

Hotel E puts you on the square with a wine lounge downstairs. Spend the days in the [wineries near Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/wine-country) and walk to dinner at the [best restaurants downtown](https://staysantarosa.com/dining).

#### An extended stay

Art House studios and suites have full kitchens and room to spread out, which suits a week or more, remote work, or a stay while visiting family in Sonoma County.

#### Travelling with kids or pets

Both hotels welcome dogs. Families tend to prefer the extra space at Art House, and the [things to do in Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/attractions), from the Schulz Museum to Safari West, are a short drive.

### Questions about where to stay in Santa Rosa

#### What is the best area to stay in Santa Rosa?

Downtown, around Old Courthouse Square. It is the most walkable part of the city, with restaurants, tasting rooms and Railroad Square nearby, and it is central for day trips to the Russian River Valley, Sonoma Valley and the coast.

#### Are there boutique hotels in downtown Santa Rosa?

Yes. Hotel E is a 39-room boutique hotel in a restored 1906 building on Old Courthouse Square, and Art House Santa Rosa is a contemporary boutique hotel with studios and suites on 7th Street.

#### Which Santa Rosa hotels have kitchens for longer stays?

Art House Santa Rosa has studios and suites with full kitchens, which makes it the downtown option for extended stays.

#### Are downtown Santa Rosa hotels pet friendly?

Both Hotel E and Art House Santa Rosa welcome dogs. Check pet policies and any fees with the hotel when you book.

#### How far are the wineries from downtown Santa Rosa?

The Russian River Valley, Sonoma Valley (Kenwood) and Dry Creek Valley tasting rooms are each roughly 20 to 30 minutes by car, and there are tasting rooms and wine bars within walking distance downtown.

#### Can I get to downtown Santa Rosa hotels without a car?

Yes. The SMART train stops at Railroad Square, a short walk from both hotels, and Charles M. Schulz Sonoma County Airport is a short drive north of downtown.

# Art House Santa Rosa | Boutique Hotel & Extended Stay

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/art-house
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Art House Santa Rosa, a boutique hotel with studios and suites: full kitchens for extended stays, local art and free breakfast in downtown Santa Rosa.

Contemporary Boutique · Downtown Santa Rosa

## Art House _Santa Rosa_Boutique Hotel with Studios & Suites

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. [Hotels](https://staysantarosa.com/hotels)
3. Art House Santa Rosa

Where Art Lives

Art House Santa Rosa is a contemporary boutique hotel built around the belief that great design and authentic local culture belong together under one roof.

The hotel's rotating collection of works by Sonoma County artists transforms guest corridors, and common areas into living gallery space, curated to feel personal, not institutional. Every piece in the gallery is for sale, with proceeds supporting local artists directly.

Modern rooms feature clean architectural lines, modern art, and warm natural materials. The design resists the impulse to impose a single aesthetic. Instead, each space holds its own point of view, a quality the city itself has always embodied.

Located in the heart of downtown Santa Rosa, Art House puts guests steps from Downtown Santa Rosa's independent restaurants, weekly farmers market on 4th Street, and the Sonoma County Museum, with wine country beginning just out the door.

- Rotating collection of original works by Sonoma County artists
- Modern rooms with natural materials and beautfiul art in every space
- In room nespresso coffee machine with condiments
- Family friendly rooms with seperated living and sleeping areas
- Concierge services to curate winery tasting arrangements
- Daily complimentary continental breakfast 6:30am - 10:00am
- Pet-friendly accommodations available

Corner Apartment Suite

The most generous 800 square foot space. The corner apartment suite makes guests feel as if they never left home. With plenty of space for luggage, living, dining, and a private bedroom, there is no better option for an extended vacation in Santa Rosa.

### Frequently Asked _Questions_

What room types does Art House offer? +

Art House offers Standard Rooms with balconies, Studios with full kitchens and approximately 600 sq ft of space, and one-bedroom Apartment Suites with full kitchens and spacious layouts up to 800 sq ft.

What are the check-in and check-out times? +

Check-in is available from 4:00 PM and check-out is at 12:00 PM. Early arrivals and late check-outs may be accommodated based on availability. Contact the front desk at [(707) 545-5400](tel:7075455400) for special requests.

Is Art House pet-friendly? +

Yes, Art House welcomes well-behaved pets. Please contact the hotel in advance to inquire about any applicable fees.

Is parking available? +

Art House has the only secured indoor parking facility in Santa Rosa. Availability is limited so guests are encoured to call and reserve in advance.

Do the studios and suites have full kitchens? +

Yes. Art House Studios include a fully equipped kitchen with modern appliances, ideal for extended stays or guests who prefer to cook. The Apartment Suites include a full kitchen, dining area, separate living room, and workspace.

Is Wi-Fi included? +

Yes, complimentary high-speed Wi-Fi is included for all guests throughout the hotel and in every room, with no hidden fees or bandwidth limits.

How far is Art House from wine country? +

Art House is located in downtown Santa Rosa, the gateway to Sonoma wine country. Russian River Valley wineries are 20–25 minutes west, Dry Creek Valley is about 25 minutes north, and Sonoma Valley is 15 minutes away. The hotel concierge can arrange private tasting appointments.

How do I make a reservation? +

Book directly at [arthousesantarosa.com](https://arthousesantarosa.com/Accommodations/?utm_source=ssrwebsite#/arthouse/) for the best available rate with no OTA fees, or call the hotel at [(707) 545-5400](tel:7075455400). The front desk is open 24/7.

### Staying at _Art House_ in downtown Santa Rosa

Art House sits in the walkable centre of Santa Rosa, which makes it a straightforward base for a Sonoma County trip. Old Courthouse Square, the 4th Street restaurants and the historic Railroad Square district are all within a short walk, and the Russian River Valley wineries begin about fifteen minutes west of the door.

The hotel is built around a rotating collection of work by artists from the region, so the building changes between visits. Studios and suites suit longer stays, and guests planning days out can use the Stay Santa Rosa guides: the [restaurant directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=dining), the [winery and brewery directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=wine) and the [attractions directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=attractions), all with current hours and directions.

# Hotel E Santa Rosa | Historic Boutique Hotel Downtown

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Hotel E Santa Rosa, a historic boutique hotel in downtown Santa Rosa: a 1906 landmark on Old Courthouse Square with 39 rooms and the Enology lounge.

Historic Beaux-Arts · Built in 1906 · Old Courthouse Square

## Hotel E _Santa Rosa_Historic Boutique Hotel in Downtown Santa Rosa

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. [Hotels](https://staysantarosa.com/hotels)
3. Hotel E Santa Rosa

A Century of Sonoma Hospitality

Built in 1906 and anchoring Old Courthouse Square, Hotel E is one of Santa Rosa's most storied addresses, a Beaux-Arts landmark that has welcomed guests through the full arc of Sonoma's history.

The hotel's 39 rooms balance the gravitas of the original architecture (high ceilings, generous moldings, the light that comes only from tall historic windows) with modern amenities that don't apologize for being contemporary. Nothing feels like a museum reproduction, because it isn't one.

The Enology Lounge is the hotel's social anchor, offering an intimate, well-curated wine program that draws on producer relationships throughout Sonoma County. It's the right place to end a day in the vineyards or to begin one before heading out to the appellation.

Valet parking, continental breakfast, and genuine dog-friendly accommodations round out a property that attends to the details without making a performance of it.

- 39 rooms in a restored 1906 Beaux-Arts building on Old Courthouse Square
- Enology Lounge, intimate wine bar with Sonoma County producer pours
- Continental breakfast included daily
- Valet parking available
- Dog-friendly throughout, genuine, not performative
- Concierge-arranged winery tastings
- Central location within walking distance of downtown dining and culture

The Enology Lounge

### Sonoma in _a glass_

The Enology Lounge is Hotel E's intimate wine bar, a room-length counter and a thoughtfully curated list of Sonoma County pours, with an emphasis on small-production, and bottles you won't find in retail. The lounge hosts occasional meet the maker events and can arrange direct visits to the producers behind every label on the menu.

Have Questions?

### Frequently Asked _Questions_

What room types does Hotel E offer? +

Hotel E has 39 thoughtfully appointed rooms across five categories: Deluxe King, Premium King (with views of Old Courthouse Square), Standard King, Deluxe Queen, and ADA-accessible Queen rooms. All feature 100% Supima Cotton linens, Luxury Villa European Down Comforters, blackout curtains, 55" 4K TVs, and eco-friendly bath amenities.

What are the check-in and check-out times? +

Check-in is at 4:00 PM and check-out is at 12:00 PM (noon). Early arrivals and late check-outs are subject to availability. Contact the front desk at [(707) 481-3750](tel:7074813750) for special accommodations. The desk is staffed 24 hours a day.

Is parking available? +

Yes, Hotel E offers secure valet parking for $25 per night. Valet is available daily from 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM. City-operated garages and metered street parking are also available nearby for guests who prefer self-parking.

Is Hotel E pet-friendly? +

Yes! Hotel E welcomes your pup for an additional $50 per stay. Old Courthouse Square is right outside the door and perfect for morning walks.

What does the continental breakfast include? +

Continental breakfast is served daily from 6:30 AM to 10:00 AM and includes fresh fruit, pastries, English muffins, bagels, and more, along with locally sourced, freshly brewed lobby coffee that's available 24/7.

What is the Enology Lounge? +

The Enology Lounge is Hotel E's in-house wine bar featuring a curated selection of award-winning Sonoma County wines by the glass, local craft beers, and light snacks. Happy hour runs daily from 5:00–7:00 PM. Look out for special events on Thursday and Friday evenings.

Is Wi-Fi included? +

Yes, Hotel E offers complimentary high-speed Wi-Fi and wired internet access throughout the property. Surf and browse freely with no hidden fees or charges.

How far is Hotel E from San Francisco? +

Santa Rosa is approximately 55 miles north of San Francisco via US-101, about 90 minutes by car depending on traffic. Charles M. Schulz Sonoma County Airport (STS) offers direct flights from Los Angeles, Las Vegas, and other West Coast cities on Alaska Airlines and Allegiant.

Are meetings and events available at Hotel E? +

Yes, Hotel E offers five versatile indoor and outdoor spaces totaling 1,000 square feet, ideal for business meetings, corporate retreats, rehearsal dinners, wedding gatherings, and small events. Contact the hotel at [reservations@hotelesantarosa.com](mailto:reservations@hotelesantarosa.com) for group inquiries.

How do I make a reservation? +

Book directly at [hotelesantarosa.com](https://hotelesantarosa.com/rooms/?utm_source=ssrwebsite#/hotele/) for the best available rate, no OTA fees and best rate guaranteed. You can also call the hotel anytime at [(707) 481-3750](tel:7074813750). The front desk is open 24 hours, 7 days a week.

### Staying at _Hotel E_ on Old Courthouse Square

Hotel E occupies a restored 1906 Beaux-Arts building at 37 Old Courthouse Square, in the middle of downtown Santa Rosa. Thirty-nine rooms sit above the Enology wine lounge, which pours Sonoma County wines by the glass and runs a daily early evening happy hour. The location means the square, the 4th Street restaurant corridor and Railroad Square are all reachable on foot.

The wider county opens up from here. Russian River Valley tasting rooms are a short drive west, Sonoma Valley runs southeast toward Kenwood, and Healdsburg sits north. Guests can plan with the [winery and brewery directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=wine), the [restaurant directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=dining) and the [attractions directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=attractions).

# Downtown Dining

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/dining
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: The best restaurants in downtown Santa Rosa: brunch, dinner and wine bars around Courthouse Square and Railroad Square, all within walking distance.

Downtown Santa Rosa

## Best Restaurants in _Downtown Santa Rosa_

Downtown Santa Rosa has quietly become one of Northern California's most interesting restaurant corridors, farm-to-table kitchens, James Beard-recognized chefs, and the kind of neighborhood wine bar that takes its list seriously.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. Downtown Dining

Kalimera Bar & Grill · B Street

#### About downtown dining

The restaurants in downtown Santa Rosa fit into a few square blocks, which is why so many visitors to Sonoma County end up staying in the city rather than driving out to it each evening. Old Courthouse Square sits at the center of it, and the kitchens fan out from there along 4th Street, Mendocino Avenue, B Street and into Railroad Square.

Density is the argument. Santa Rosa is the largest city in the county, so it carries a working restaurant scene rather than a handful of destination rooms, and most of it is close enough together that you can change your mind at the door and be somewhere else five minutes later. Wine country dinners usually involve a car, a route and a designated driver. Here you leave the car where it is, walk out, and eat.

[Browse the full restaurant list →](https://staysantarosa.com/dining-list)

#### A practical way to plan the week

Book the one dinner that matters before you arrive, and leave the rest open. Tables at the busiest downtown rooms go first on Friday and Saturday evenings, but midweek the walkable core absorbs walk-ins comfortably. Guests at [Hotel E on Old Courthouse Square](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) and at [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) are close enough to try the door before committing to a table.

29restaurants mapped

4wine appellations within reach

2downtown hotels

Where to start

### Three rooms on and around _4th Street_

The square does most of the heavy lifting. These three sit within a few minutes of each other and cover three different kinds of evening.

[Browse the full restaurant list →](https://staysantarosa.com/dining-list)

#### Augie's French

4th Street · Stark Reality Restaurants

Classic French bistro cooking in an intimate, polished room from James Beard-nominated restaurateurs Mark and Terri Stark. The quiet end of a downtown evening.

On the list →

#### Stark's Steak & Seafood

Adams Street · Oyster bar

A proper steakhouse with a live oyster bar, just off the square. This is the room people book when the meal itself is the occasion.

On the list →

#### Bird & The Bottle

1055 4th Street

Modern tavern cooking built around small plates, with Asian, Jewish, Southern and East Coast flavors on one menu. Suits a group that wants to keep ordering.

On the list →

Further out

### Beyond the square, and _after dark_

Beer Baron Bar & Kitchen · 4th Street

#### Push a block or two out and the range widens

Four kitchens with nothing in common except the same short walk. That range inside one district is a large part of what makes people ask where to eat in Santa Rosa and then never leave the downtown grid.

- Kalimera Bar & Grill on B Street, for Greek and Mediterranean cooking.
- Eddie's Kitchen on Mendocino Avenue, on the Italian side.
- El Coqui, also on Mendocino Avenue, for Puerto Rican food.
- Beer Baron Bar & Kitchen on 4th Street, a gastropub with a deep craft beer and whiskey list.

Belly Left Coast Kitchen & Taproom · 4th Street

#### Late night, and eating around a wine country day

Downtown does not shut down the moment dinner service winds up. Ausiello's 5th Street Bar & Grill is the neighborhood answer after a concert or a long drive back from the coast, and on 7th Street HanBul Korean BBQ and Haku Sushi sit close together. Belly Left Coast Kitchen keeps the bar side of the evening going near the square.

Sonoma County grows a great deal of what its restaurants cook, so menus shift with what is available and harvest, late summer into fall, is the busiest stretch at the tables as well as in the vineyards. The rhythm that works is simple: spend the day out among the [wineries near Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/wine-country), come back into town, and eat within walking distance of where you are sleeping. Hours move by season, so check the [restaurant directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=dining) before you walk.

### Common questions about eating in Santa Rosa

#### Where should I eat in downtown Santa Rosa?

Start on 4th Street and around Old Courthouse Square, where Augie's French, Loro di Napoli and Bird & The Bottle sit close together, with Stark's Steak & Seafood just off the square on Adams Street. Beer Baron Bar & Kitchen is a few doors along 4th Street. The full directory is on the restaurant list page.

#### What restaurants are walking distance from Old Courthouse Square?

Most of the downtown scene. Augie's French, Loro di Napoli, Bird & The Bottle and Belly Left Coast Kitchen are on 4th Street, Stark's is on Adams Street, Kalimera Bar & Grill is on B Street, and Eddie's Kitchen and El Coqui are on Mendocino Avenue. Railroad Square sits a short walk further west.

#### Do I need reservations for restaurants in Santa Rosa?

For weekend dinners at the busier downtown rooms, yes, and more so during harvest, which runs late summer into fall. Midweek you can usually walk in. Book the one dinner that matters and leave the others flexible.

#### Where do locals eat in Santa Rosa?

Away from the obvious. El Coqui and Eddie's Kitchen on Mendocino Avenue, Kalimera on B Street, HanBul Korean BBQ and Haku Sushi on 7th Street, and Ausiello's for a late one. The dining guide article goes into more detail on this.

#### Are there restaurants open late in Santa Rosa?

Yes. Ausiello's 5th Street Bar & Grill, Belly Left Coast Kitchen on 4th Street, and HanBul Korean BBQ and Haku Sushi on 7th Street all run later than a standard dinner service. Hours vary by night and by season, so check the restaurant map before you set out.

### Eating in _downtown Santa Rosa_

Most of the restaurants worth planning an evening around sit within a few blocks of Old Courthouse Square, along 4th Street and out toward Railroad Square. That density is the reason downtown works so well as a base: you can have coffee on Mendocino Avenue, lunch in Railroad Square, a tasting flight in the afternoon and dinner on 4th Street without moving the car.

The range is wider than most visitors expect. There is French bistro cooking, a steak and oyster house, wood-fired Neapolitan pizza, Puerto Rican and Caribbean plates, Greek and Mediterranean grilling, sushi, Korean barbecue and a Jewish deli, alongside the farm to table kitchens that Sonoma County is known for. Several rooms are run by chefs who have cooked here for decades, and menus change with what the county is growing.

For hours, ratings and directions, use the [restaurant directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=dining), which pulls its information from each restaurant's own Google Business Profile. Staying nearby makes all of it easier: our hotels, [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) and [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e), are inside this walking radius.

# Wineries Near Santa Rosa

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/wine-country
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Wineries near Santa Rosa and Sonoma wine tasting: Russian River Valley, Sonoma Valley and Dry Creek tasting rooms 20 to 30 minutes from downtown.

Sonoma County, California

## Wineries Near Santa Rosa _& Sonoma Wine Tasting_

Santa Rosa sits at the center of Sonoma County's wine map, three of California's most celebrated appellations within a 30-minute drive, and a fourth practically in the city limits.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. Wine & Beer

Sonoma County Wine Country

#### About wine & beer near Santa Rosa

The wineries near Santa Rosa are not clustered in one direction, which is the single most useful thing to understand before you plan a trip to Sonoma County. The city sits where four appellations meet, so the vineyards begin west of town, east of town, and north toward Healdsburg, all from the same starting line.

That geometry is the practical case for basing here rather than in one of the smaller wine towns. From a room in downtown Santa Rosa, you are not committed to a region on arrival. You pick a direction each morning and come back to the same bed at night.

[Browse the full winery list →](https://staysantarosa.com/wine-country-list)

#### How to plan a tasting day that works

Pick one direction per day and stay in it. Three tastings is a comfortable day and four is the practical ceiling, because the appointments run longer than people expect. Book ahead wherever a reservation is required, and settle the driving question before the first pour, either with a designated driver or a car service.

22wineries

9breweries

4appellations

By direction

### Three ways out of town, _three appellations_

Pick one direction per day and stay in it. Each of these begins within about half an hour of Old Courthouse Square.

[Browse the full winery list →](https://staysantarosa.com/wine-country-list)

West

#### Russian River Valley

Pinot Noir & Chardonnay

Fog moves inland and the season runs long and cool. Balletto on Occidental Road, Benovia and DeLoach in the heart of it, Kendall-Jackson on Fulton Road. Take this direction first if you have one day.

On the list →

East

#### Sonoma Valley & the hills

Elevation & views

Matanzas Creek grows lavender alongside the vines, Kunde tastes in caves cut into the hillside, and Paradise Ridge holds a hilltop with a sculpture grove. A fair trade of convenience for a clear day.

On the list →

North

#### Dry Creek & Alexander Valley

Toward Healdsburg

Dry Creek Vineyard, Wilson and Ridge Lytton Springs run up the narrower valley with Zinfandel doing the talking. Alexander Valley spreads wider and warmer. Treat it as a full day.

On the list →

Without a car

### Tasting rooms and taprooms _inside the city_

Enology at Hotel E · Old Courthouse Square

#### Downtown Santa Rosa tasting rooms

You do not need to leave the city to taste. Several producers keep rooms in the downtown grid, which turns an arrival afternoon or a rained-out morning into something usable.

- D'Argenzio Winery, pouring its own label in town.
- Stonemason Cellars, a small downtown room.
- Enology, the wine lounge beneath [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) at 37 Old Courthouse Square.

Enology is the easiest of the three to fold into an evening, and the [Hotel E page](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) covers what to expect. Both Hotel E and [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) put you inside that walking radius.

Russian River Brewing Company · 4th Street

#### Santa Rosa breweries

Sonoma County is as serious about beer as it is about wine, and Santa Rosa is where most of that happens. Russian River Brewing Company on 4th Street is the name that draws people from out of state, and it sits right in the downtown core. Shady Oak Barrel House on 1st Street is the other walkable option.

Beyond the downtown blocks, Cooperage, Fogbelt, Moonlight and HenHouse all operate in and around the city, with Lagunitas down in Petaluma worth building a drive around. A brewery afternoon makes a good counterweight in the middle of a tasting-heavy trip, and the [winery and brewery list](https://staysantarosa.com/wine-country-list) covers which vineyard stops pair with it.

### Common questions about wine tasting near Santa Rosa

#### How many wineries can you visit in a day?

Three is comfortable, four is the practical limit. Tastings run longer than people plan for, and driving between appellations eats the rest. Staying in one direction each day is what makes three or four realistic instead of rushed.

#### Do you need reservations for wine tasting in Sonoma?

At many wineries, yes, particularly for seated or estate tastings and especially during harvest. Some rooms still take walk-ins. Check the [wine directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=wine) for current hours before you set out, and book the visits you care most about in advance.

#### Can you walk to wineries from downtown Santa Rosa?

You can walk to tasting rooms rather than to vineyards. D'Argenzio Winery, Stonemason Cellars and the Enology lounge at Hotel E are all in the downtown grid. The estates themselves are a short drive out in every direction.

#### Which Sonoma appellation is closest to Santa Rosa?

Four appellations meet around the city, so no single one has it to itself. Russian River Valley begins just west of town, Bennett Valley and the Sonoma Valley run east, and Dry Creek and Alexander Valley open out to the north around Healdsburg.

#### What is the best time of year for wine tasting in Sonoma?

Harvest, which runs late summer into fall, is the most atmospheric and the busiest. Spring and early summer are quieter and the tasting rooms have more time for you. Winter suits a downtown base, where the tasting rooms are a walk rather than a drive.

Santa Rosa & Sonoma County

### Sonoma _Wineries_

Santa Rosa sits inside four of Sonoma County's most celebrated AVAs, Sonoma Valley, Russian River Valley, Dry Creek Valley, and Alexander Valley, with world-class tasting rooms a short drive from downtown Santa Rosa. From cave tours to cult Pinot Noir, here's where to taste.

Sonoma Valley

Matanzas Creek Winery

Sonoma Valley · Bennett Valley AVA

Rustic country charm meets refined quality in Bennett Valley, Chardonnay, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc, and Pinot Noir from a stunning estate known for its lavender fields and sweeping valley views.

[matanzascreek.com →](https://www.matanzascreek.com)

St. Francis Winery

Sonoma Valley · Kenwood

Voted best tasting room in the region, award-winning wines paired with chef-crafted bites in a beautiful Sonoma Valley setting. Known for rich reds and a genuinely warm hospitality experience.

[stfranciswinery.com →](https://www.stfranciswinery.com)

Kunde Winery

Sonoma Valley · Kenwood · 1,850 acres

A fifth-generation family estate with 1,850 acres of vineyards stretching from valley floor to mountain ridge. Cave tours, cave tastings, and one of Sonoma Valley's most impressive estate experiences.

[kunde.com →](https://www.kunde.com)

Nearby Favorites

Balletto Vineyards

Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa

A family farm turned world-class winery, cool-climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from the heart of the Russian River Valley, with a relaxed tasting room and genuinely welcoming staff.

[ballettovineyards.com →](https://www.ballettovineyards.com)

Benovia Winery

Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa

Small-production Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from some of the Russian River Valley's most celebrated vineyards, precise, cellar-worthy wines from a winery that earns serious attention.

[benoviawinery.com →](https://www.benoviawinery.com)

Paradise Ridge Winery

Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa

Hilltop views, sculpture gardens, and estate wines. Paradise Ridge combines art, nature, and Sonoma winemaking in one of the area's most scenically distinctive settings.

[paradiseridge.com →](https://www.paradiseridge.com)

Dry Creek Valley

Dry Creek Vineyard

Dry Creek Valley · Healdsburg

The benchmark for Dry Creek Zinfandel, a pioneering estate that helped define the appellation. The picnic grounds and relaxed tasting room make it one of the valley's most pleasant afternoons.

[drycreekvineyard.com →](https://www.drycreekvineyard.com)

Wilson Artisan Wines

Dry Creek Valley · Healdsburg

Family-owned and focused on old-vine Zinfandel, Petite Sirah, and Rhône varieties from the Dry Creek and Alexander valleys, bold, food-friendly wines with a personal touch.

[wilsonartisanwines.com →](https://www.wilsonartisanwines.com)

Our Staff Favorites

Larson Family Winery

Sonoma Valley · Carneros

A fun, family-friendly estate with a petting zoo, bocce courts, and seriously good Zinfandel and Merlot, the kind of relaxed afternoon winery that earns its place on any Sonoma itinerary.

[larsonfamilywinery.com →](https://larsonfamilywinery.com)

Breathless Wines

Russian River Valley · Healdsburg

Sparkling wines made in the traditional method from Russian River Valley fruit, elegant, celebratory, and worth seeking out. A distinctive addition to any Sonoma wine itinerary.

[breathlesswines.com →](https://www.breathlesswines.com)

Ridge Winery

Dry Creek Valley · Lytton Springs

Old-vine Zinfandel-based blends with the depth and track record that earns a place in serious cellars worldwide. The Lytton Springs estate is Ridge's Dry Creek anchor. Tasting here is a rare experience.

[ridgewine.com →](https://www.ridgewine.com)

Bricoleur Vineyards

Russian River Valley · Windsor

A modern estate winery combining farm-fresh hospitality with cool-climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. On-site farm-to-table dining and a beautiful setting make it a full-day destination.

[bricoleurvineyards.com →](https://bricoleurvineyards.com)

Merriam Vineyards

Russian River Valley · Healdsburg

A boutique family winery known for elegant, estate-grown Pinot Noir and an elevated tasting experience, intimate, unhurried, and focused on wine that speaks for itself.

[merriamvineyards.com →](https://www.merriamvineyards.com)

DeLoach Vineyards

Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa

Certified biodynamic and a pioneer in Sonoma sustainability, DeLoach produces expressive Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, and Zinfandel from organically farmed estate vineyards in the Russian River Valley.

[deloachvineyards.com →](https://deloachvineyards.com/)

Santa Rosa & Sonoma County

### Craft _Breweries_

Santa Rosa has been dubbed the Microbrew Capital of the U.S., with Russian River leading a scene that spans barrel-aged sours, hop-forward IPAs, and Belgian-style ales. All locations are within a short drive of downtown Santa Rosa.

★ Must Visit

Russian River Brewing Co.

725 4th St, Santa Rosa · 5 min walk from Hotel E

The brewery that put Sonoma on the global craft beer map. World-famous for Pliny the Elder (double IPA) and the cult annual release of Pliny the Younger (triple IPA, March 20–April 2). Year-round pours include Belgian ales, barrel-aged sours, and California IPAs. Second location with brewery tours in Windsor.

Signatures: Pliny the Elder · Blind Pig IPA · Supplication · STS Pils

[russianriverbrewing.com →](https://www.russianriverbrewing.com)

Downtown

Cooperage Brewing Co.

Multiple Santa Rosa locations · 8 min walk

A downtown Santa Rosa staple with an energetic taproom and a rotating lineup of hazy IPAs, sours, and creative small-batch brews. Pinball machines, a pool table, and rotating food trucks round out the experience.

Signatures: Keg Slayer IPA · Bow Down · rotating sours

[cooperagebrewing.com →](https://www.cooperagebrewing.com)

CA-Grown Hops

Fogbelt Brewing Co.

1305 Cleveland Ave, Santa Rosa · 10 min drive

Named for the coastal fog that nourishes Sonoma's redwoods, Fogbelt uses exclusively California-grown hops. The urban-hip taphouse pours reliable blonde ales, IPAs, and stouts alongside innovative seasonals.

Signatures: Atlas Blonde · Del Norte IPA · Armstrong Stout

[fogbeltbrewing.com →](https://www.fogbeltbrewing.com)

Barrel-Aged

Shady Oak Barrel House

420 1st St, Santa Rosa · 8 min walk

Sonoma County's home for wild ales and barrel-aged sours, complex, tart, and endlessly rotating. A cool casual taproom with the kind of experimental program that draws serious beer travelers from across the state.

Signatures: Wild ales · Barrel-aged sours · Rotating experimental

[shadyoakbarrelhouse.com →](https://shadyoakbarrelhouse.com)

Since 1992

Moonlight Brewing Co.

3350 Coffey Ln, Santa Rosa · 12 min drive

A Santa Rosa institution since 1992, small, hands-on, and fiercely independent. Moonlight brews traditional lagers and ales with artisan precision. Death & Taxes and Reality Czeck are among the county's most beloved year-round pours.

Signatures: Death & Taxes · Reality Czeck · Bombay By Boat IPA

[moonlightbrewing.com →](https://moonlightbrewing.com)

Sebastopol

Crooked Goat Brewing

The Barlow, Sebastopol · 20 min drive

A passion project turned People's Choice Award winner at The Barlow in Sebastopol. Innovative IPAs and rotating seasonals in a family-friendly setting, and not available in stores, so the taproom is the only way to taste it.

Signatures: Hazy Hazy Hazy IPA · Coffee & Cream Ale

[crookedgoatbrewing.com →](https://www.crookedgoatbrewing.com)

New · Nov 2025

Fieldwork Brewing Co.

Montgomery Village, Santa Rosa · 12 min drive

Berkeley's acclaimed small-batch brewery opened its Santa Rosa taproom in November 2025, bringing an ever-changing lineup of fresh hazy IPAs alongside Neapolitan and Detroit-style pizza. Spacious indoor and outdoor seating.

Signatures: Rotating hazy IPAs · fresh small-batch releases

[fieldworkbrewing.com →](https://fieldworkbrewing.com)

Listings

We list wineries and breweries at no charge. To request adding or removing your business, or to make a change, please contact [hello@staysantarosa.com](mailto:hello@staysantarosa.com).

### Tasting from a _Santa Rosa_ base

Santa Rosa sits at the meeting point of four of Sonoma County's celebrated growing regions. The Russian River Valley wraps around the city to the west and is the reason so many Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producers are within fifteen minutes of downtown. Sonoma Valley runs southeast toward Kenwood and Glen Ellen. Dry Creek Valley and Alexander Valley sit north around Healdsburg, where the focus turns to Zinfandel, Cabernet Sauvignon and old vines.

Because the appellations fan out in different directions, it is worth choosing one per day rather than crossing the county twice. A morning in Russian River, lunch back in town and an afternoon in Sonoma Valley is a comfortable day. Healdsburg deserves its own. If you would rather not drive at all, several tasting rooms are inside Santa Rosa itself, and the [Enology lounge at Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) pours Sonoma County by the glass on the ground floor.

Beer matters here too. Santa Rosa has been called the microbrew capital of the country, and the taprooms range from a globally known brewpub on 4th Street to barrel-aged and wild ale houses. The [winery and brewery directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=wine) lists every one of them with current hours, and [our wine country guide](https://staysantarosa.com/wine-country) explains what each direction does best.

# Things to Do

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/attractions
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Things to do in Santa Rosa: the Charles Schulz Museum, Luther Burbank Gardens, redwoods, the Sonoma Coast and the best events this season.

Santa Rosa & Sonoma County

## Things to Do in _Santa Rosa_

From ancient redwoods and rugged coastline to world-class performance venues and beloved local landmarks, there's a lot to discover beyond the tasting room.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. Attractions

Downtown Santa Rosa & Sonoma County

#### About Santa Rosa attractions

Most lists of things to do in Santa Rosa open with wine, and then stop. That undersells the place. Santa Rosa is the largest city in Sonoma County, California, and it carries the museums, parks and civic history that come with being the county's center of gravity rather than one of its weekend destinations.

Two names anchor the city's reputation, and neither is a winery. Charles M. Schulz drew Peanuts here for decades, and Luther Burbank ran his plant breeding work from a garden on Santa Rosa Avenue. Around those sit an old-growth redwood reserve, a wildlife preserve, two large parks on the eastern edge of town, and a downtown compact enough to cover on foot between Old Courthouse Square and the Railroad Square historic district.

[Browse the full attractions list →](https://staysantarosa.com/attractions-list)

#### For a rainy day or an off-season visit

Winter and the shoulder seasons are when the indoor half of the city earns its place. The Schulz Museum, the Museum of Sonoma County and the downtown tasting rooms are all under a roof, and the walk between them is short enough to do in weather. Quieter months also mean easier tables and more attention wherever you go.

8attractions mapped

30restaurants mapped

2downtown hotels

Museums & culture

### The three visitors _travel for_

Neither of the names that anchor this city is a winery. Both left institutions behind that are still open, and the county museum sits downtown between them.

[Browse the full attractions list →](https://staysantarosa.com/attractions-list)

Museum

#### Charles M. Schulz Museum

Hardies Lane

Built around the work of the Peanuts creator, who lived and drew in Santa Rosa for decades. It treats the strip as a body of work rather than as nostalgia, and it holds children's attention properly.

On the list →

Gardens

#### Luther Burbank Home & Gardens

Santa Rosa Avenue

The horticulturist's house and the experimental garden he worked in. If you have ever eaten a plum or a potato variety he developed, the garden is a stranger and better visit than it sounds.

On the list →

Downtown

#### Museum of Sonoma County

7th Street

Art exhibitions and the county's own history under one roof, a few streets from the square. It slots easily into a morning that ends with lunch nearby.

On the list →

Outdoors

### Where the city stops and _the hills start_

Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve · Guerneville

#### Hiking and open space near Santa Rosa

Trione-Annadel State Park, reached from Channel Drive, gives you miles of trail rising straight off the eastern edge of town, on foot or by bike. Spring Lake Park on Newanga Avenue sits alongside it and is the gentler option. The two connect, so you can start soft and go as far as you feel like.

Further out, Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve at Guerneville holds old-growth coast redwoods, and it pairs naturally with a Russian River day. Safari West on Porter Creek Road is the outlier, a wildlife preserve running guided tours across open country.

Bodega Bay · Sonoma Coast

#### Day trips from Santa Rosa

The city's real advantage is what it is close to. Three directions take you somewhere completely different, and each works as a day out with a return to the same room.

- West to the Sonoma Coast and Bodega Bay, for cliffs, cold water and a different climate entirely.
- Northwest along the Russian River, through redwoods and small river towns on its way to the sea.
- North to Healdsburg, a smaller town built around its own plaza, and the gateway to two more appellations.

Each can be done without an early start. The [wineries near Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/wine-country) page covers what to add on the way.

### Common questions about visiting Santa Rosa

#### What is Santa Rosa California known for?

Wine country, but also two figures who worked here. Charles M. Schulz drew Peanuts in Santa Rosa for decades and is remembered at the Schulz Museum on Hardies Lane, and Luther Burbank ran his plant breeding work from the home and gardens on Santa Rosa Avenue. It is also the largest city in Sonoma County.

#### Is Santa Rosa worth visiting?

Yes, particularly as a base. Four wine appellations meet around the city, the coast and the Russian River are both a day trip away, and the downtown holds museums, restaurants and tasting rooms inside a walkable few blocks.

#### What is there to do in Santa Rosa with kids?

The Charles M. Schulz Museum is the strongest draw for families. Safari West runs guided tours across a wildlife preserve and has tent cabins on site, and Spring Lake Park on Newanga Avenue gives you easy paths and a lake for the quieter part of the day.

#### How far is Santa Rosa from the ocean?

The Sonoma Coast lies west of the city and Bodega Bay is the usual destination, comfortably reachable as a day trip and back. Armstrong Redwoods at Guerneville sits along the same general route if you want to combine redwoods with the coast.

#### What is there to do in downtown Santa Rosa at night?

The downtown core around Old Courthouse Square holds restaurants, bars and tasting rooms within a few blocks of each other, with Railroad Square a short walk west. The Luther Burbank Center for the Arts on Mark West Springs Road programs touring theater and music.

## Santa Rosa Attractions & Annual Events

The complete list of museums, gardens, parks, coastline and the annual events worth planning a trip around, filterable by the kind of day you want.

2. [Attractions](https://staysantarosa.com/attractions)
3. Attractions & Events List

Arts & Culture

Santa Rosa _Landmarks_

Performing Arts

Luther Burbank Center for the Arts

50 Mark West Springs Rd · 5 min drive

The North Bay's premier performing arts center, Broadway tours, world-class music, comedy, dance, and speaker events in a 1,600-seat main hall. Over 50,000 children served annually through its education programs.

[lutherburbankcenter.org →](https://www.lutherburbankcenter.org)

Museum

Charles M. Schulz Museum

2301 Hardies Ln · 10 min drive

Dedicated to the life and work of Santa Rosa's most famous resident, the creator of Peanuts. Original comic strips, biographical exhibits, a recreation of Schulz's studio, and the beloved Snoopy's Home Ice rink next door.

[schulzmuseum.org →](https://schulzmuseum.org)

Historic Site

Luther Burbank Home & Gardens

204 Santa Rosa Ave · 5 min walk

The meticulously preserved home and experimental gardens of America's celebrated horticulturist, who developed over 800 new plant varieties. Free to visit and a genuinely peaceful downtown stop.

[lutherburbank.org →](https://lutherburbank.org)

Historic District

Railroad Square Historic District

Historic 3rd St · 10 min walk

Built around the restored 1903 Northwestern Pacific Railroad depot, this charming district is lined with antique shops, independent restaurants, and coffee houses, and the starting point for the SMART commuter train.

[railroadsquare.net →](https://www.railroadsquare.net)

Wildlife

Safari West

3115 Porter Creek Rd · 15 min drive

A 400-acre African wildlife preserve, dubbed the "Sonoma Serengeti", with giraffes, rhinos, zebras, cheetahs, and nearly 900 animals roaming free. Guided jeep tours and glamping tents available.

[safariwest.com →](https://www.safariwest.com)

Museum

Museum of Sonoma County

425 7th St · 4 min walk

Rotating art exhibitions and historical displays exploring Sonoma County's cultural past and present, and conveniently right around the corner from the downtown hotels.

[museumsc.org →](https://museumsc.org)

Outdoors

Nature & _Coast_

State Reserve

Armstrong Redwoods State Reserve

Guerneville · 35 min drive

Ancient coastal redwoods, some over 1,400 years old and 300 feet tall, tower above quiet forest trails near Guerneville. One of the most accessible old-growth redwood groves in Northern California.

[parks.ca.gov →](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=450)

Coastal

Bodega Bay

Sonoma Coast · 50 min drive

The dramatic Sonoma Coast, fresh Dungeness crab, rugged headland hikes, sheltered coves, and the village made famous by Hitchcock's The Birds. The drive alone through the coastal hills is worth the trip.

[bodegabay.com →](https://www.bodegabay.com)

State Park

Trione-Annadel State Park

Channel Dr, Santa Rosa · 15 min drive

Over 5,000 acres of forests, meadows, and streams with 40+ miles of hiking, biking, and equestrian trails right on Santa Rosa's eastern edge. Lake Ilsanjo is a popular fishing and picnic destination in the interior.

[parks.ca.gov →](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=480)

Regional Park

Spring Lake Regional Park

393 Violetti Rd · 15 min drive

Santa Rosa's 320-acre backyard, a swimming lagoon with lifeguards, boat rentals, hiking trails, and a hands-on natural history center. Popular on warm weekends with locals and visitors alike.

[parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov →](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/spring-lake-regional-park)

River

Russian River

Guerneville · 30 min drive

In summer, the Russian River comes alive with canoeing, kayaking, swimming, and fishing. The Guerneville stretch is the most popular. Rent a canoe and float downstream through redwood-lined banks.

[sonomacounty.com →](https://www.sonomacounty.com/outdoor-activities/russian-river)

Adventure

Hot Air Ballooning

Various launch sites · Sonoma County

Drift above the vineyards at sunrise. Sonoma County's ballooning is among the most celebrated in California. Several outfitters launch from Santa Rosa, floating over the Russian River Valley and wine country hills.

[sonomacounty.com →](https://www.sonomacounty.com/outdoor-activities/hot-air-ballooning)

The world's most coveted triple IPA returns for two weeks only at Russian River Brewing's Santa Rosa and Windsor brewpubs. Lines form before dawn, open daily 11 AM–10 PM, three pours per guest, bottles available on-site only. A genuine Sonoma County pilgrimage.

### Ready to _explore?_

Every museum, park, restaurant, tasting room and hotel in one place, with addresses, hours and directions.

### Beyond the vineyards in _Sonoma County_

Wine is the reason most people come, and it is rarely the part they talk about afterwards. Santa Rosa is where Charles Schulz drew Peanuts for decades, and the museum built around his work is a short drive north of downtown. Luther Burbank spent fifty years breeding plants on a city block that is now a preserved home and garden. The Museum of Sonoma County holds both art and county history a few minutes' walk from Old Courthouse Square.

Outdoors, the county changes character quickly. Trione-Annadel State Park puts oak woodland and forty miles of trail in the hills at the edge of town. Spring Lake is the local lake loop. An hour west, Armstrong Redwoods holds old-growth coast redwoods, and beyond that the Sonoma Coast runs from Bodega Bay north along bluffs and coves. Safari West, north of the city, keeps a wildlife preserve you can tour and even sleep in.

The [attractions directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=attractions) shows hours, ratings and directions for these places.

# Rainy Day in Santa Rosa | Indoor Things to Do

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/blog-rainy-day-santa-rosa
Updated: 2026-10-22
Summary: Indoor things to do in Santa Rosa on a rainy day: the Schulz Museum, Snoopy's Home Ice, the Museum of Sonoma County and kids' museum, with hours and prices.

Attractions

## A Rainy Day in Santa Rosa: _Indoor Things to Do_

Peanuts, an ice rink, art and history downtown, and a museum built for kids. Just avoid Tuesdays.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. [Blog](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)
3. Rainy Day in Santa Rosa | Indoor Things to Do

[← All stories](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)

Stay Santa Rosa · Oct 22, 2026

Winter is the rainy season in Sonoma County, and a wet day can scramble a plan built around vineyards and redwood trails. Santa Rosa handles it better than most wine country towns. It has a museum devoted to the creator of Peanuts, an ice rink he built, a downtown art and history museum and a hands-on children's museum, all within a short drive of each other. The one catch is the calendar: several of these close on Tuesdays, so check the day before you plan around them.

### Charles M. Schulz Museum

Charles Schulz lived and worked in Santa Rosa for more than thirty years, and his museum is the city's best rainy-day stop. Expect original strips, a recreation of his studio and a changing line-up of exhibitions. This winter that includes:

- _Inking History_, through January 10, 2027.
- _Blanket Statements: The Philosophies of Linus_, through March 10, 2027.
- _Why Can't I Have a Normal Dog?_, from November 11, 2026, to July 12, 2027.

**Hours:** Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. It is **closed every Tuesday**. **Admission:** $15 adults, $10 seniors 62 and over, $7 students and youth ages 4 to 18, free for children 3 and under. Tickets are sold on arrival only. The museum is at 2301 Hardies Lane, about ten minutes from downtown, with free parking.

Inside the Charles M. Schulz Museum, about ten minutes from downtown.

### Snoopy's Home Ice

Across the street from the museum, the ice arena Schulz built for the town is the most active way to spend a wet afternoon. Public skating is priced by session type:

- **Weekday** (1.5 hours): $8 admission, $2 skate rental.
- **Night** (1.5 hours): $10 admission, $2 skate rental.
- **Weekend and holiday** (2 hours or more): $14 for ages 12 and over, $12 for children 11 and under, $4 skate rental.

Admission is sold in person only, starting 30 minutes before each session, and session times are posted on the rink's online schedule. The rink is at 1667 West Steele Lane. In November and December it also runs holiday public sessions and shows.

### Museum of Sonoma County

Right downtown at 425 7th Street, the Museum of Sonoma County mixes art exhibitions with the history of the county. The _Santa Rosa History_ gallery is ongoing. This season brings the _37th Annual Artistry in Wood_ show (November 21, 2026, to January 31, 2027) and _Golden California: Landscape Masters of the American West_ (December 12, 2026, to April 11, 2027). The 30th annual Día de los Muertos exhibition closes on November 29.

**Hours:** Wednesday to Sunday, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., so it is **closed Monday and Tuesday**. **Admission:** $12 adults, $10 seniors 62 and over, $6 students, free for children 13 and under. EBT cardholders get in free through Museums for All.

### Children's Museum of Sonoma County

With younger kids, the Children's Museum at 1835 West Steele Lane, on the same road as the rink, is built for burning off energy indoors. It opens at 9 a.m. most days and closes at 4 p.m., with a later 6 p.m. close on Thursdays. It is **closed Tuesdays**. Admission is $18 for adults and children, $15 for seniors 62 and over, military and teachers, and free for infants 11 months and younger.

### A rainy-day plan from downtown

Put the indoor stops on the north side together, and keep the evening downtown.

1. **Morning:** the Schulz Museum when it opens, then lunch.
2. **Afternoon:** a skating session at Snoopy's Home Ice across the street, or the Children's Museum with small kids.
3. **Late afternoon:** back downtown for the Museum of Sonoma County before its 5 p.m. close (Wednesday to Sunday).
4. **Evening:** a pint at Russian River Brewing Co. on 4th Street, then dinner from our [downtown food guide](https://staysantarosa.com/blog-santa-rosa-culinary-scene).

#### Good to know

- Tuesday is the hardest day for a rainy-day plan: the Schulz Museum, the Museum of Sonoma County and the Children's Museum are all closed.
- The Schulz Museum and Snoopy's Home Ice both sell admission on arrival only.
- All three museums close on Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day.

### Stay close to the indoor options

On a wet day, the less time spent driving the better. [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) is in a historic building right on Old Courthouse Square, with continental breakfast, an evening happy hour to come back to and valet parking. [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) is a few blocks away on 7th Street. From either one, the Museum of Sonoma County and downtown dinner are on foot, and the Schulz Museum is a short drive.

#### Plan your stay downtown

Browse hotels, restaurants, wineries and attractions, all in one place.

[Open the directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory)

# Santa Rosa Itinerary | Museums, Redwoods & the Sonoma Coast

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/blog-santa-rosa-attractions
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: A Santa Rosa itinerary for first-timers: museums, redwoods and the Sonoma Coast, plus family days out and things to do at night in Santa Rosa.

Attractions

## Santa Rosa Itinerary: Museums, Redwoods & _the Sonoma Coast_

Peanuts, redwoods, giraffes and the Pacific. What to do in and around Santa Rosa when you're not at the table.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. [Blog](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)
3. Santa Rosa Itinerary | Museums, Redwoods & the Sonoma Coast

[← All stories](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)

Stay Santa Rosa · Sep 24, 2026

Wine gets most of the attention, but Santa Rosa has plenty to fill the hours in between. The city was home to two of America's best-known names, Charles Schulz and Luther Burbank, and it sits within an hour of ancient redwoods, a wild coastline and one of the most unusual wildlife parks in California.

### In town

#### Charles M. Schulz Museum

The creator of Peanuts lived and worked in Santa Rosa for more than thirty years. The museum, about ten minutes from downtown, holds original strips, a recreation of his studio and rotating exhibitions. Across the street, Snoopy's Home Ice is the ice arena Schulz built for the town.

#### Luther Burbank Home & Gardens

A short walk from Old Courthouse Square, the preserved home and gardens of the horticulturist who developed more than 800 plant varieties. The gardens are free to wander, and docent-led tours cover the house in season.

#### Museum of Sonoma County

Right downtown on 7th Street, with rotating art and history exhibitions about the county's past and present. An easy hour before lunch.

#### Railroad Square

West of the highway, the historic district grew up around the restored railroad depot. It is lined with antique shops, independent restaurants and bars, and the SMART train station is right there.

### Wildlife and open space

**Safari West**, fifteen minutes north, is a 400-acre wildlife preserve with giraffes, rhinos, cheetahs and hundreds of other animals. Guided safari tours in open-air vehicles are the way to see it, and you can even stay overnight in a tent cabin.

On the east side of town, **Trione-Annadel State Park** has more than forty miles of hiking and biking trails over 5,000 acres, and neighboring **Spring Lake Regional Park** has a lifeguarded swimming lagoon and boat rentals in summer.

Armstrong Redwoods, about 35 minutes west of downtown.

### Day trips

**Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve**, near Guerneville, is about thirty-five minutes west. Some of the trees are more than 1,400 years old, and the main loop is flat and easy. In summer, pair it with a paddle on the **Russian River**, where outfitters rent canoes and kayaks.

Keep going west and you reach **Bodega Bay** and the Sonoma Coast in under an hour: headland hikes, sheltered coves, fresh crab and the town Hitchcock made famous in The Birds.

### Evenings and early mornings

The **Luther Burbank Center for the Arts** brings Broadway tours, concerts and comedy to a 1,600-seat hall on the north side of town. And if you can handle an early start, a sunrise **hot air balloon** flight over the vineyards is one of the most memorable ways to see the county.

#### Before you go

- Safari West tours and balloon flights book up, so reserve ahead.
- Check park conditions after heavy rain or during fire season.
- The coast is often cooler and foggier than town. Bring a layer.

### Plan your days

The [attractions directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=attractions) lists addresses and directions for everything here, and the [attractions guide](https://staysantarosa.com/attractions) covers more ideas for a first visit or a fifth. Our hotels, [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) and [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e), are a short walk from the museum, the Burbank gardens and the square.

#### Plan your stay downtown

# Where to Eat in Santa Rosa | A Local Food & Brunch Guide

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/blog-santa-rosa-culinary-scene
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Where to eat in Santa Rosa: a local food guide to brunch spots, dinner, Railroad Square restaurants and late-night bites in downtown Santa Rosa.

Dining

## Where to Eat in Santa Rosa: _A Local Food Guide_

From early espresso to midnight sushi, a full day of eating within a few blocks of Old Courthouse Square.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. [Blog](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)
3. Where to Eat in Santa Rosa | A Local Food & Brunch Guide

[← All stories](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)

Stay Santa Rosa · Sep 24, 2026

Santa Rosa sits in the middle of one of the richest farming regions in the country. The produce, cheese, oysters and wine that end up on menus in San Francisco often start here, and the downtown restaurants get it first. The result is a food scene that is serious without being fussy, and almost all of it is walkable from Old Courthouse Square.

Here is how to eat your way through a day.

### Morning

Start small at **Crook's Coffee** on Mendocino Avenue, the closest good espresso to the square, open early on weekdays. If you want a proper breakfast, **Omelette Express** and **Dierks Café** are local institutions with more than a thousand reviews each, and **Café Mimosa** on College Avenue does brunch seven days a week.

### Lunch

Lunch is where downtown shows its range. **Grossman's Noshery & Bar** serves elevated Jewish deli, with pastrami and latkes worth the walk to Wilson Street. **Mac's Deli** on 4th Street is the quick, classic option. For something brighter, **Kalimera** on B Street grills Mediterranean and Turkish plates with a strong bar program.

Pizza people should know about **Loro di Napoli**, which fires true Neapolitan pies in a wood oven, and **Jackson's Bar & Oven** in Railroad Square, which shows up on nearly every local best-of list.

Augie's French, on 4th Street.

### Dinner

Much of downtown's fine dining traces back to one couple. Mark and Terri Stark, James Beard-nominated restaurateurs, run several of the city's best rooms:

- **Bird & The Bottle**, a modern tavern and one of Santa Rosa's most consistently top-rated restaurants.
- **Stark's Steak & Seafood**, a proper steakhouse with a live oyster bar and a deep Sonoma wine list.
- **Augie's French**, their newest, a classic bistro in an intimate room on 4th Street.

Beyond the Stark family, **The Spinster Sisters** does imaginative California farm-to-table cooking in a warm room, **Eddie's Kitchen** leans Italian with standout tuna dishes, and **Darbar Kitchen** covers Indian and Nepalese cooking with real regional depth. **Lococo's** is the Railroad Square pick for old-school Italian; reserve ahead on weekends.

### Late night

Santa Rosa stays up later than you might expect. **Haku Sushi** and **HanBul Korean BBQ**, side by side on 7th Street, both keep their kitchens open until midnight. For drinks, **J&A Lounge** has live music and creative cocktails, **The Goose & Fern** pours British ales in a converted Victorian, and **Beer Baron** pairs a good tap list with food it takes seriously.

#### Good to know

- Book dinner ahead on Friday and Saturday, especially at the Stark restaurants.
- Many downtown kitchens close between lunch and dinner. Check hours before you walk over.
- Local farmers' markets run most weeks of the year and are a good way to graze.

### Plan your table

The [restaurant directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=dining) shows current hours, ratings and directions for every place mentioned here, and the [downtown dining guide](https://staysantarosa.com/dining) goes deeper on neighborhoods. Staying downtown makes all of it easier; our hotels, [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) and [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e), are both inside the walking radius.

#### Plan your stay downtown

Browse hotels, restaurants, wineries and attractions, all in one place.

[Open the directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory)

# Wine Tasting in Sonoma from Santa Rosa | Russian River Guide

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/blog-santa-rosa-wine-country-launch-pad
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Wine tasting from Santa Rosa: a route guide to Russian River Valley wineries, Sonoma Valley tasting rooms and wineries with food near Santa Rosa.

Wine Country

## Wine Tasting from Santa Rosa: _Russian River & Sonoma Valley_

Four celebrated valleys, one downtown base. How to plan wine country days from the center of Sonoma County.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. [Blog](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)
3. Wine Tasting in Sonoma from Santa Rosa | Russian River Guide

[← All stories](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)

Stay Santa Rosa · Sep 24, 2026

Sonoma County is big. It runs from the San Pablo Bay to the Mendocino line and from the Mayacamas Mountains to the Pacific, and it holds more than a dozen wine appellations. Pick the wrong base and you spend your trip in the car. Pick Santa Rosa and almost every major valley is a short drive in a different direction, with a real downtown to come back to at night.

That is the case for Santa Rosa in one sentence: it sits in the middle. Here is how to use it.

### West: the Russian River Valley

The Russian River Valley starts on the western edge of town. Morning fog rolls in from the coast and burns off by midday, which is why the valley is known for cool-climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. Most estates are twenty to twenty-five minutes from downtown.

- **Balletto Vineyards**, a family farm turned winery with a relaxed tasting room and serious Pinot.
- **DeLoach Vineyards**, certified biodynamic and one of the valley's sustainability pioneers.
- **Benovia Winery**, small-production, cellar-worthy Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
- **Paradise Ridge**, hilltop views and a sculpture garden a few minutes from town.
- **Kendall-Jackson Wine Estate**, seated tastings and walking garden tours at the brand's Santa Rosa home.

**Martin Ray** sits on Laguna Road on the west side of Santa Rosa. Head north toward Windsor and Healdsburg for **Bricoleur Vineyards**, **Merriam Vineyards** and the traditional-method sparkling wines at **Breathless**.

### Southeast: Sonoma Valley and Kenwood

Highway 12 runs southeast out of Santa Rosa into the Sonoma Valley. The first stretch, around Kenwood, is only about twenty minutes away and holds some of the county's best-known tasting rooms.

- **St. Francis Winery** known for rich reds and chef-paired food and wine tastings.
- **Kunde Winery**, a fifth-generation estate with cave tours across 1,850 acres.
- **Matanzas Creek**, in the quiet Bennett Valley, famous for its lavender fields as much as its Sauvignon Blanc.
- **Coursey Graves**, a boutique Bennett Valley estate on Santa Rosa's southeast edge with a food-paired tasting experience.

### North: Dry Creek and Alexander valleys

Twenty-five minutes up Highway 101 puts you in the Healdsburg area. Dry Creek Valley is Zinfandel country; Alexander Valley is warmer and built for Cabernet.

- **Dry Creek Vineyard**, the benchmark for Dry Creek Zinfandel, with picnic grounds out front.
- **Ridge Lytton Springs**, old-vine Zinfandel blends with a worldwide reputation.
- **Wilson Artisan Wines**, bold Zinfandel and Petite Sirah from a family operation.

Most estates on this list are twenty to thirty minutes from downtown.

### No car? Taste downtown

You don't need to leave the city to drink well. A handful of tasting rooms sit inside the downtown grid, close enough to walk between after dinner.

- **Stonemason Cellars** on Davis Street, a small room with knowledgeable, personable staff.
- **Trecini Winery** on Beaver Street, open early in the week, so check before you go.
- **D'Argenzio Winery** on Cleveland Avenue, with a music-forward feel and a long family history in wine.
- **Enology**, the wine lounge at [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) on Old Courthouse Square, pouring Sonoma County by the glass.

### And then there's the beer

Santa Rosa is one of the best beer towns in California. **Russian River Brewing Co.** on 4th Street is the one people cross the country for, home of Pliny the Elder and the annual release of Pliny the Younger. Nearby, **Shady Oak Barrel House** specializes in wild and barrel-aged sours, and **Cooperage**, **Fogbelt**, **HenHouse** and **Moonlight** round out a strong local lineup.

#### Plan it well

- Many estates are reservation only, especially on weekends. Book a day or two ahead.
- Pick one direction per day. Three or four tastings is plenty.
- Hire a driver or use a tour service if everyone wants to taste.
- Harvest, late August into October, is the busiest and most atmospheric time of year.

### Why come back to town

This is the other half of the argument. After a day in the valleys, Santa Rosa gives you a walkable downtown with serious restaurants, cocktail bars and live music, and you can leave the car parked until morning. Our hotels, [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) and [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e), are both a short walk from Old Courthouse Square.

For current hours, ratings and directions for every winery and brewery mentioned here, use the [winery and brewery directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory?cat=wine), or browse the [wine and beer guide](https://staysantarosa.com/wine-country).

#### Plan your stay downtown

Browse hotels, restaurants, wineries and attractions, all in one place.

[Open the directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory)
