# Thanksgiving Weekend in Santa Rosa 2026 | What's Open

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/blog-thanksgiving-weekend-santa-rosa
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Thanksgiving 2026 in Santa Rosa: which museums close on Nov 26, the Schulz Museum Family Fun Weekend, holiday skating and the Winter Lights kickoff.

Seasonal

## Thanksgiving Weekend in Santa Rosa: _What's Open and What's On_

What closes on the holiday, what opens after it, and how to spend four days with downtown Santa Rosa as your base.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. [Blog](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)
3. Thanksgiving Weekend in Santa Rosa 2026 | What's Open

[← All stories](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)

Stay Santa Rosa · Oct 21, 2026

Thanksgiving falls on **Thursday, November 26, 2026**, and the long weekend that follows is one of the easiest times to visit Santa Rosa. The harvest is in, the holiday season starts downtown, and a few local museums plan special programming around the break. A few places also close on the holiday itself, so a little planning goes a long way. Here is what is open, what is on, and how to shape four days from a downtown base.

### What closes on Thanksgiving Day

Plan Thursday around family, a long meal and a walk, because several of the city's main attractions take the day off.

- **Charles M. Schulz Museum:** closed on Thanksgiving Day.
- **Museum of Sonoma County:** closed on Thanksgiving Day and on the Friday after Thanksgiving.
- **Children's Museum of Sonoma County:** closed on Thanksgiving.

Restaurants set their own holiday hours, and many take reservations only for a set Thanksgiving menu. If you want a table on Thursday, call ahead rather than counting on walking in. Our [downtown food guide](https://staysantarosa.com/blog-santa-rosa-culinary-scene) is a good place to start the shortlist.

### Friday: Peanuts and the holiday kickoff

The Schulz Museum runs a **Family Fun Weekend** from 11 a.m. on Friday, November 27, through 5 p.m. on Saturday, November 28. It is a good fit for a day after the big meal, especially with kids along. The museum is open 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Fridays and 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekends. Admission is $15 for adults, $10 for seniors 62 and over, $7 for students and youth ages 4 to 18, and free for children 3 and under. Tickets are sold on arrival only, with no advance sales.

Two exhibitions are on during the holiday weekend. _Inking History_ runs through January 10, 2027, and _Why Can't I Have a Normal Dog?_ opens on November 11, 2026. The museum is at 2301 Hardies Lane, about ten minutes from downtown, with free parking.

Back downtown, the holiday season traditionally begins the day after Thanksgiving. Downtown Santa Rosa's **Winter Lights** program opens with a free tree lighting celebration on Old Courthouse Square, with live entertainment, holiday treats, photos with Santa and a skating show starring Snoopy. In 2025 the lighting ran from 4 to 7 p.m. on the Friday after Thanksgiving. The 2026 times had not been posted when we published this guide, so check the Downtown Santa Rosa events calendar before you go.

The Schulz Museum runs a Family Fun Weekend over the Thanksgiving break.

### Saturday: skating and wine country

Across the street from the museum, **Snoopy's Home Ice** at 1667 West Steele Lane runs holiday public skating sessions through November and December. Weekend and holiday sessions last two hours or more and cost $14 for ages 12 and over, $12 for children 11 and under, plus $4 for skate rental. Admission is sold in person only, starting 30 minutes before each session, and the session times are posted on the rink's online schedule.

If the weather is clear, Saturday is also a good day for wine country. The Russian River Valley, Sonoma Valley, Dry Creek Valley and Alexander Valley are each roughly 20 to 30 minutes by car from downtown. Book tastings ahead on a holiday weekend, and settle on a driver before you set out. Our [wine country guide](https://staysantarosa.com/blog-santa-rosa-wine-country-launch-pad) covers the routes.

### Sunday: last chance for Día de los Muertos

The Museum of Sonoma County reopens for the weekend after its two-day closure. Its hours are Wednesday to Sunday, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., and **Sunday, November 29, is the final day** of the 30th annual Día de los Muertos exhibition, which opened on September 5. The _37th Annual Artistry in Wood_ show also opens on November 21 and runs through January 31, 2027, so one visit covers both.

Admission is $12 for adults, $10 for seniors 62 and over, $6 for students, and free for children 13 and under. The museum is at 425 7th Street, an easy walk from the square, which makes it a relaxed last stop before the drive home.

#### Good to know

- Thanksgiving is Thursday, November 26, 2026. The Schulz Museum, the Museum of Sonoma County and the Children's Museum are all closed that day.
- The Museum of Sonoma County is also closed Friday, November 27.
- The Schulz Museum is closed every Tuesday, if you are extending the trip into the following week.
- Downtown Santa Rosa posts the Winter Lights schedule; confirm the 2026 tree lighting time before you plan Friday evening.

### Where to stay for the long weekend

Staying downtown means the tree lighting, the museum on 7th Street and dinner are all on foot, with the Schulz Museum and the rink a short drive away. [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) is in a historic building right on Old Courthouse Square, with continental breakfast in the morning, an evening happy hour and valet parking for the car. [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) is a few blocks away on 7th Street. Either one puts you in the middle of the holiday kickoff without needing to move the car.

#### Plan your stay downtown

Browse hotels, restaurants, wineries and attractions, all in one place.

[Open the directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory)

# Whale Watching on the Sonoma Coast | Santa Rosa

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/blog-whale-watching-sonoma-coast
Updated: 2026-10-28
Summary: When gray whales pass the Sonoma Coast, where to watch from shore at Bodega Head and beyond, volunteer weekends, spotting tips and a day trip from Santa Rosa.

Seasonal

## Whale Watching on the Sonoma Coast: _A Day Trip from Santa Rosa_

Gray whales pass the headlands from December to May. Bodega Head is under an hour from downtown.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. [Blog](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)
3. Whale Watching on the Sonoma Coast | Santa Rosa

[← All stories](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)

Stay Santa Rosa · Oct 28, 2026

Twice a year, some 20,000 gray whales travel along the California coast, south to the lagoons of Baja California in winter and north to the Bering Sea in spring. The Sonoma Coast is one of the easiest places to watch them from land, and its best-known lookout, Bodega Head, is under an hour's drive from downtown Santa Rosa. Here is when to go, where to stand and how to turn it into a day trip.

### When to see gray whales on the Sonoma Coast

According to the Marine Mammal Center, gray whales pass California heading **south in December and January**, and heading **north from mid-February to early May**, with most of the northbound whales seen in March and April. Mothers and calves usually travel last, so they are often seen through April and into early May. Sonoma County Regional Parks notes that mothers with first-year calves tend to swim closer to shore than the adults ahead of them.

Sonoma County Tourism puts the peak whale-watching months at January through May. Humpback whales also show up off the coast in spring, summer and fall.

### Bodega Head

Bodega Head, part of Sonoma Coast State Park, is a headland about four miles long and a mile wide that juts out into the Pacific just west of Bodega Bay. Its high bluffs give long views over the water, and California State Parks lists it for excellent views of migrating whales.

- **Hours:** day use from 8 a.m. to sunset.
- **Trail:** the Bodega Head Trail runs 1.89 miles along the bluffs.
- **Fees:** State Parks lists a $10 per vehicle day-use fee at its campground parking areas only.
- **Whale Watch volunteers:** on weekends from January through Mother's Day, trained volunteers are on the headland, generally from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., to answer questions about the whales and the migration.

The bluffs and rocks are unstable, so stay on the trails and respect the fences and warning signs.

Bluff-top views on the Sonoma Coast near Bodega Bay.

### More places to watch from shore

Highway 1 north of Bodega Bay passes a string of headlands. Sonoma County Tourism and Sonoma County Regional Parks recommend these:

- **Goat Rock Beach, Jenner:** at the mouth of the Russian River, with gray whales offshore and harbor seals on the beach.
- **Fort Ross State Historic Park:** watch from the cliffs around the historic fort.
- **Stillwater Cove Regional Park:** the Stillwater Bluff Trail leads to a vista point.
- **Salt Point State Park:** several trails end at cliff-top viewpoints.
- **Gualala Point Regional Park:** Whale Watch Point, on the bluff above the beach, is the park's main viewing spot. Go early and you may see the first whale of the day.

The county regional parks charge a parking fee, and members park free.

### Seeing them from the water

For a closer look, whale-watching trips leave from Bodega Bay. Sonoma County Tourism points to operators including Bodega Bay Sport Fishing Center, Miss Vic Sportfishing and North Bay Charters. Trips depend on sea conditions, so check schedules and book directly with the operator.

### How to spot a gray whale

The Marine Mammal Center's tips for watching from shore:

- Go in the morning, when the sun is in the east and behind you.
- Bring binoculars and sweep the horizon slowly from left to right and back.
- Look for spouts. A gray whale's breath makes a puffy, often heart-shaped spout. If you see one, keep watching the same spot, as the whale is likely to surface again.
- Gray whales have no dorsal fin. Look for a low hump and a row of six to twelve small bumps along the back, and mottled gray-and-white skin.

### A whale-watching day from Santa Rosa

1. **Morning:** drive west to Bodega Head and arrive with the sun behind you. On a weekend from January on, find the volunteers on the headland.
2. **Midday:** lunch in Bodega Bay, then follow Highway 1 north to Goat Rock Beach and Jenner.
3. **Afternoon:** one more bluff-top stop at Fort Ross or Salt Point if the light holds, or head back inland along the Russian River.
4. **Evening:** dinner downtown. Our [downtown food guide](https://staysantarosa.com/blog-santa-rosa-culinary-scene) has ideas, and our [Santa Rosa itinerary](https://staysantarosa.com/blog-santa-rosa-attractions) covers more coast and redwood days.

#### Good to know

- Southbound gray whales pass in December and January; northbound whales from mid-February to early May.
- Whale Watch volunteers are at Bodega Head on weekends from January through Mother's Day.
- Bodega Head is open for day use from 8 a.m. to sunset.
- Bring binoculars and a warm layer, and stay back from bluff edges.

### Stay in Santa Rosa, watch on the coast

Santa Rosa puts the coast and wine country within an easy drive, with a real downtown to come back to. [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) sits in a historic building on Old Courthouse Square, with continental breakfast for an early start, an evening happy hour and valet parking. [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) is a few blocks away on 7th Street. Either one makes a comfortable base for a morning on the bluffs and an evening downtown.

#### Plan your stay downtown

Browse hotels, restaurants, wineries and attractions, all in one place.

[Open the directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory)

# Wine & Food Affair 2026 | Plan It from Santa Rosa

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/blog-wine-food-affair-santa-rosa
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Plan the Wine & Food Affair, Nov 7 to 8, 2026, from Santa Rosa: how check-in works, ticket rules, a two-day valley route and where to stay downtown.

Wine Country

## Wine & Food Affair 2026: _Plan the Weekend from Santa Rosa_

Dozens of wineries, three pours and a food pairing at each, and a downtown base twenty to thirty minutes from all of it.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. [Blog](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)
3. Wine & Food Affair 2026 | Plan It from Santa Rosa

[← All stories](https://staysantarosa.com/blog)

Stay Santa Rosa · Oct 14, 2026

The first weekend of November is one of the best food and wine weekends on the Sonoma County calendar. The **28th annual Wine & Food Affair**, run by the Wine Road, takes place **Saturday and Sunday, November 7 and 8, 2026**, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. each day. Dozens of wineries pour their wines alongside a dish made to match, and you move between them at your own pace. Here is how it works, and how to plan the weekend with downtown Santa Rosa as your base.

### How the Wine & Food Affair works

When you buy a ticket, you choose a **check-in winery**. That is where you start: you pick up your tasting glass and wristband there, and after that you can visit the participating wineries in any order. Each winery pours a minimum of three wines and serves a featured food pairing, often a recipe the winery has developed for the event. The Wine Road keeps past pairings in its online recipe collection, which is worth a look if a dish wins you over.

For 2026 the Wine Road lists 43 participating wineries, with more expected. They are spread across the **Alexander Valley, Dry Creek Valley, Russian River Valley and the Healdsburg area**. A few only take part on one day: Limerick Lane Cellars is Saturday only and Dutcher Crossing is Sunday only, and Sunday-only tickets are also offered. Tickets are sold through CellarPass from the Wine Road's ticket page.

### Rules to know before you book

- **21 and over only.** Wine Road events do not admit children, babies or minors, and photo ID is required with no exceptions.
- **Designated driver tickets** are available for drivers 21 or older. They include the food pairings but no wine tasting, and come with a different wristband color.
- **Groups of eight or more** cannot be accommodated at participating wineries during the event.
- **Check-in is capped** at 50 check-ins per winery, so popular starting points fill up.
- **All sales are final** and non-refundable.

Early November light in the vineyards north of Santa Rosa.

### Why Santa Rosa works as a base

The participating valleys sit north and west of the city, and the Russian River Valley, Dry Creek Valley and Alexander Valley are each roughly 20 to 30 minutes by car from downtown Santa Rosa. That puts you in reach of every corner of the event without moving hotels, and it leaves Saturday night free for a proper dinner in town rather than a long drive back from somewhere quieter.

It also helps on price. Tasting fees have come down in Sonoma County: the 2026 Silicon Valley Bank direct-to-consumer wine report found the county's average standard tasting fee fell by $7 to $47 in 2025. An event ticket that bundles tastings and food at dozens of wineries is a good way to sample widely in one weekend.

### A simple two-day plan

**Saturday.** Pick a check-in winery in the valley you want to explore most and get there close to 11 a.m., before the cap fills. Stay within one valley for the afternoon. Three or four wineries is plenty when each one pours three wines with food, and the doors close at 4 p.m. Head back to Santa Rosa, rest, then walk to dinner downtown.

**Sunday.** Switch valleys. If you started in the Russian River Valley, try Dry Creek or Alexander Valley on day two, or use Sunday for the one-day-only wineries. Finish in Healdsburg for a walk around the plaza before the short drive back.

**Getting around.** Decide on your driver before you buy. A designated driver ticket still includes every food pairing, so the driver gets a real day out too.

#### Good to know

- Dates: November 7 and 8, 2026, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. each day.
- Wine Road Insider members get a discount on tickets; details are on the Wine Road site.
- Choose your check-in winery when you buy, and plan your route around it.

### Where to stay for the weekend

A downtown base keeps the evenings easy. [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) is in a historic building right on Old Courthouse Square, with continental breakfast before you set out and valet parking for the car. [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) is a few blocks away on 7th Street. Both put the restaurants in our [downtown food guide](https://staysantarosa.com/blog-santa-rosa-culinary-scene) on foot, and our [wine country guide](https://staysantarosa.com/blog-santa-rosa-wine-country-launch-pad) covers the valleys for the rest of the year.

#### Plan your stay downtown

Browse hotels, restaurants, wineries and attractions, all in one place.

[Open the directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory)

# About Stay Santa Rosa | Our Swallow Logo & Story

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/about
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Why Stay Santa Rosa uses a swallow as its logo: the migratory swallows of the Laguna de Santa Rosa, travelers flying in for better weather, and the nature of Sonoma County.

About

## About Stay Santa Rosa

A general travel guide to Santa Rosa and Sonoma County, and the story behind our swallow.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. About

Stay Santa Rosa was created by [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) and [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) as a general travel guide to the city we call home: where to eat, where to taste, what to see, and how to make the most of a few days in Sonoma County.

### Our logo: the swallow

The mark at the heart of our logo is a swallow in flight, drawn in a single continuous line. We chose it because swallows are some of Santa Rosa's most faithful visitors. Every spring they return to the same wetlands, fields and eaves, and every year they remind us that this is a place worth coming back to.

### The swallows of the Laguna de Santa Rosa

Just west of downtown, the Laguna de Santa Rosa is the largest freshwater wetland complex on the northern California coast and the largest tributary of the Russian River. In 2010 it was recognized as a Wetland of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention.

Each spring the Laguna fills with migratory swallows. Tree swallows, violet-green swallows, barn swallows and cliff swallows arrive after wintering farther south, some as far as Mexico, Central America and South America. Through spring and summer they skim low over the marshes and open water catching insects, nest in tree cavities, bridges and barns, and raise their young before heading south again as the days shorten. Watching them sweep across the water at dusk is one of the quiet pleasures of a Santa Rosa evening.

### What the swallow means to us

Like the swallows, most of our visitors fly in from somewhere else. They come to Santa Rosa to escape the fog, the cold or the city, for warm days and cool evenings, and for the food, wine and experiences that make Sonoma County worth the journey. The swallow is a symbol of that trip: leaving home in search of better weather and something memorable, and finding it here.

It is also our homage to the nature of Sonoma County. The vineyards, redwoods, coastline and wetlands that surround Santa Rosa are what make this corner of California so remarkable, and the swallow is a small, familiar part of that landscape. We hope it reminds you to look up while you're here.

### Plan your own migration

Start with the [directory](https://staysantarosa.com/directory) of restaurants, wineries, breweries and attractions, browse the [journal](https://staysantarosa.com/blog) for longer guides, or read about our hotels, [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) and [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house). Questions or corrections are always welcome at [hello@staysantarosa.com](mailto:hello@staysantarosa.com).

# Accessibility Statement

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/accessibility
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: Our commitment to keeping staysantarosa.com usable for every visitor, the standards we work to, and how to tell us when something on the site gets in your way.

Accessibility

## Accessibility Statement

How we build this site to stay usable for everyone, and how to tell us when it is not.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. Accessibility

Last updated September 3, 2026

- The standard we work to
- What is in place today
- Known limits
- Giving us feedback
- Accessibility at the hotels

We want every visitor to be able to read these guides and plan a trip, whatever device or assistive technology they use. Accessibility is treated as part of the build, not an afterthought, and the site is revisited as it grows.

### The standard we work to

We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at Level AA. That covers text contrast, keyboard access, meaningful structure for screen readers, and content that adapts to smaller screens and larger text.

### What is in place today

- Semantic headings and landmarks, so screen reader users can move through a page by structure.
- Text alternatives for meaningful images, and decorative images marked so they are skipped.
- Colour contrast checked against the WCAG AA thresholds for body text and interface labels.
- Keyboard access to navigation, filters, search fields and map controls.
- Labels and accessible names on buttons, toggles and form fields.
- Layouts that reflow to a single column on phones without horizontal scrolling.
- Animation that respects the reduced motion setting in your operating system. If you have that setting turned on, entrance animations, parallax and slow zooms are switched off.
- Interactive maps paired with the same information in text, so nothing is available only inside the map.

### Known limits

Some parts of the site depend on services provided by others, including the map library, map imagery and embedded video. We cannot always control how those behave with assistive technology. Where a map is used, the same places are also listed as text cards with addresses, hours, phone numbers and links, so the content is never locked inside the map.

Business hours and ratings in the guides come from third party sources and may occasionally read awkwardly in a screen reader when a business publishes unusual hours.

### Tell us when something gets in your way

If any part of this site is difficult to use, we want to hear about it. Tell us the page, what you were trying to do, and the device, browser or assistive technology you were using, and we will work on it. Email [hello@staysantarosa.com](mailto:hello@staysantarosa.com) or see the [contact page](https://staysantarosa.com/contact).

If you need information from this site in another format, or help completing a booking, hotel staff can assist by phone or in person.

### Accessibility at the hotels

This statement covers the website. For accessible rooms, entrances, parking and facilities at [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house) or [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e), contact the hotel directly so the team can match you with the right room and answer questions about the building before you arrive.

# Privacy Policy

URL: https://staysantarosa.com/privacy
Updated: 2026-10-21
Summary: How Stay Santa Rosa collects, uses and protects information on this website, including analytics, cookies, third party booking engines and your privacy rights in California.

Legal

## Privacy Policy

What this website collects, what it does not, and the choices you have.

1. [Home](https://staysantarosa.com/)
2. Privacy Policy

Last updated September 25, 2026

- Who operates this site
- Information this site collects
- Maps, fonts and third parties
- Booking and reservations
- Google Analytics
- Cookies
- Your privacy rights
- Security and retention
- Changes to this policy

This policy explains what information staysantarosa.com collects, why it is collected, and what choices you have. Stay Santa Rosa is a general travel guide created and operated by [Hotel E Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/hotel-e) and [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/art-house). It features the two hotels alongside restaurants, wineries and attractions in the surrounding area. It is not a booking system, and no reservation is created or stored on this site.

### Who operates this site

Stay Santa Rosa was created by Hotel E and Art House Santa Rosa as a general travel guide, and the two hotels run and operate staysantarosa.com. In this policy, "we", "us" and "our" mean Hotel E Santa Rosa (37 Old Courthouse Square, Santa Rosa, CA) and Art House Santa Rosa (620 7th Street, Santa Rosa, CA) acting as operators of this website. Each hotel also runs its own hotel website and booking engine, which are covered by that hotel's own privacy policy rather than this one.

### Information this site collects

This website does not ask you to create an account, and it does not include a contact form, newsletter signup, or payment page. In normal use we do not collect names, email addresses, phone numbers or payment details through this site.

Like most websites, the server that delivers these pages records standard technical information each time a page is requested. That can include your IP address, browser and device type, the page you requested, the page that referred you, and the date and time. This information is used to keep the site working, diagnose errors, and understand which guides visitors find useful. It is used only to operate and improve Stay Santa Rosa.

#### Analytics

This site uses Google Analytics to understand how visitors use the guides. See Google Analytics below for what it collects and how to opt out.

#### Local storage

Some pages remember small preferences in your browser, such as which filter you last used on a guide. That information stays on your device, is not transmitted to us, and can be cleared at any time through your browser settings.

### Maps, fonts and other third party services

Several pages use services provided by others. When a page loads content from one of these services, that service receives the request and can see technical information such as your IP address, in line with its own privacy policy.

- **Map tiles and libraries.** The interactive guides load map imagery and the Leaflet mapping library from third party content networks.
- **Google Maps links.** Directions links and business profile links open Google Maps in a new tab. Business hours, ratings and addresses shown in the guides are drawn from each business's own public Google Business Profile.
- **Web fonts.** Typefaces are served by Google Fonts.
- **Video and imagery.** Some photography is provided by Hotel E, Art House Santa Rosa and featured businesses.

We do not control these services and we are not responsible for their practices. Review their policies if you want to understand how they handle data.

### Google Analytics

We use Google Analytics 4, a web analytics service provided by Google LLC, to count visits and see which pages, guides and links are used most. When you load a page, the Google tag (gtag.js) runs in your browser and sends Google information such as the pages you view, how long you stay, the links you click, the site that referred you, your approximate location (city or region, derived from your IP address), and your device, browser, operating system and screen size. Google Analytics 4 does not log or store full IP addresses.

To tell visits apart, Google Analytics sets first party cookies in your browser, named _ga and _ga_NWT0RRXS42, which contain a random identifier and can last up to two years unless you delete them. We see this information only as aggregated reports and do not use it to identify you. We do not send Google your name, email address or other information that directly identifies you, and analytics data is not combined with hotel guest or reservation records.

Google processes this data under its own terms and privacy policy. You can learn more at [How Google uses information from sites that use its services](https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites). To opt out, you can block or delete cookies in your browser, use a content blocker, or install the [Google Analytics opt-out browser add-on](https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout). The guides work normally with analytics blocked.

### Booking and hotel reservations

Booking buttons on this site hand you off to the booking engine used by Hotel E or Art House Santa Rosa, on that hotel's own domain. Although the same hotels operate Stay Santa Rosa, any information you enter there, including guest details and payment information, is collected and processed by that hotel and its booking provider under the hotel's own privacy policy, not this one. This site does not receive, see or store your reservation details.

### Cookies

This site does not use advertising cookies. The cookies it sets come from Google Analytics, described above; embedded third party services may set their own. You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings; the guides and maps will continue to work, though some conveniences may reset between visits.

### Children

This website is intended for a general audience planning travel. It is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children.

### Your privacy rights

Apart from the analytics data described above, this site does not collect personal information, so there is usually little for us to retrieve, correct or delete. If you believe we hold information about you, or you have a question about this policy, email [hello@staysantarosa.com](mailto:hello@staysantarosa.com) and we will respond.

#### California residents

California residents have rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended, including the right to know what personal information a business collects, to request its deletion, to correct inaccurate information, and not to be discriminated against for exercising those rights. The analytics data described above is the main category of personal information collected through this site (online identifiers and internet activity), and it is used only to measure and improve the site. We do not sell personal information, and we do not use it for cross-context behavioral advertising. To make a request, email [hello@staysantarosa.com](mailto:hello@staysantarosa.com).

#### Do Not Track

This site does not currently respond to Do Not Track browser signals. Google Analytics measures visits to this site only; you can opt out using the options in the Google Analytics section.

### Security and retention

Server logs are kept only as long as they are useful for operating and improving the site, then discarded. Google Analytics data is kept for the retention period set in our Google Analytics account (Google offers 2 or 14 months), then deleted automatically. No system is perfectly secure, but the site is served over an encrypted connection and holds no guest records.

### Changes to this policy

If this policy changes, the revised version will be posted here with a new date at the top of the page. Continued use of the site after a change means you accept the updated policy.

### Contact

Questions about this policy can be sent through the [contact page](https://staysantarosa.com/contact), or by email to [hello@staysantarosa.com](mailto:hello@staysantarosa.com).

## Wineries and breweries

### Balletto Vineyards

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa
- Website: https://www.ballettovineyards.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#balletto-vineyards

A family farm turned world-class winery, cool-climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from the heart of the Russian River Valley, with a relaxed tasting room and genuinely welcoming staff.

### Benovia Winery

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa
- Website: https://www.benoviawinery.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#benovia-winery

Small-production Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from some of the Russian River Valley's most celebrated vineyards, precise, cellar-worthy wines from a winery that earns serious attention.

### Breathless Wines

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Healdsburg
- Website: https://www.breathlesswines.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#breathless-wines

Sparkling wines made in the traditional method from Russian River Valley fruit, elegant, celebratory, and worth seeking out. A distinctive addition to any Sonoma wine itinerary.

### Bricoleur Vineyards

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Windsor
- Website: https://bricoleurvineyards.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#bricoleur-vineyards

A modern estate winery combining farm-fresh hospitality with cool-climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. On-site farm-to-table dining and a beautiful setting make it a full-day destination.

### Cooperage Brewing Co.

- Type: Brewery
- Area: Multiple Santa Rosa locations
- Website: https://www.cooperagebrewing.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#cooperage-brewing-co

A downtown Santa Rosa staple with an energetic taproom and a rotating lineup of hazy IPAs, sours, and creative small-batch brews. Pinball machines, a pool table, and rotating food trucks round out the experience.

### Coursey Graves Estate Winery

- Type: Winery
- Area: Bennett Valley · Santa Rosa · Estate
- Address: 6860 Serenity Way, Santa Rosa, CA
- Website: https://www.courseygraves.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#coursey-graves-estate-winery

A boutique Bennett Valley estate in Santa Rosa consistently rated among the best tasting room experiences near Santa Rosa. The Cellarius Kitchen Experience pairs estate wines with chef-prepared courses in a setting that wine lovers describe as unlike anything else in Sonoma.

### Crooked Goat Brewing

- Type: Brewery
- Area: The Barlow, Sebastopol
- Website: https://www.crookedgoatbrewing.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#crooked-goat-brewing

A passion project turned People's Choice Award winner at The Barlow in Sebastopol. Innovative IPAs and rotating seasonals in a family-friendly setting, and not available in stores, so the taproom is the only way to taste it.

### D'Argenzio Winery

- Type: Urban Tasting Room
- Area: Urban Tasting Room · Santa Rosa · Downtown
- Address: 1301 Cleveland Ave Ste a, Santa Rosa, CA
- Phone: (707) 546-2466
- Website: https://www.dargenziowinery.com
- Hours: Thu 5–8 PM · Sat–Sun 12–5 PM
- Map: https://maps.google.com/?cid=14337380938011327876
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#d-argenzio-winery

A downtown Santa Rosa winery with an eclectic, music-forward vibe, one of the city's most unique tasting room experiences. Winemaker Raymond D'Argenzio is known for his personality as much as his wines. Great for date night or a girls' afternoon.

### DeLoach Vineyards

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa
- Website: https://deloachvineyards.com/
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#deloach-vineyards

Certified biodynamic and a pioneer in Sonoma sustainability, DeLoach produces expressive Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, and Zinfandel from organically farmed estate vineyards in the Russian River Valley.

### Dry Creek Vineyard

- Type: Winery
- Area: Dry Creek Valley · Healdsburg
- Website: https://www.drycreekvineyard.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#dry-creek-vineyard

The benchmark for Dry Creek Zinfandel, a pioneering estate that helped define the appellation. The picnic grounds and relaxed tasting room make it one of the valley's most pleasant afternoons.

### Fieldwork Brewing Co.

- Type: Brewery
- Area: Montgomery Village, Santa Rosa
- Website: https://fieldworkbrewing.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#fieldwork-brewing-co

Berkeley's acclaimed small-batch brewery opened its Santa Rosa taproom in November 2025, bringing an ever-changing lineup of fresh hazy IPAs alongside Neapolitan and Detroit-style pizza. Spacious indoor and outdoor seating.

### Fogbelt Brewing Co.

- Type: Brewery
- Address: 1305 Cleveland Ave Ste A, Santa Rosa, CA
- Phone: (707) 978-3400
- Website: https://www.fogbeltbrewing.com
- Hours: Taproom hours vary
- Map: https://maps.google.com/?cid=9845997062775705815
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#fogbelt-brewing-co

Named for the coastal fog that nourishes Sonoma's redwoods, Fogbelt uses exclusively California-grown hops. The urban-hip taphouse pours reliable blonde ales, IPAs, and stouts alongside innovative seasonals.

### Fogline Vineyards

- Type: Winery
- Area: Sonoma Coast · Santa Rosa Adjacent
- Website: https://www.foglinevineyards.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#fogline-vineyards

Small-production Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from fog-cooled Sonoma Coast vineyards, the kind of precise, terroir-driven winemaking that earns top Yelp ratings from guests who visit once and join the wine club on the spot.

### HenHouse Brewing Co.

- Type: Brewery
- Address: 322 Bellevue Ave, Santa Rosa
- Website: https://www.henhousebrewing.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#henhouse-brewing-co

Bold, inventive, and sustainability-focused, HenHouse rolls out a constantly changing lineup of hazy IPAs, rich stouts, and passion-project brews. Rotating food trucks and a welcoming taproom make it a full afternoon destination.

### Hook & Ladder Vineyard

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa
- Website: https://www.hookandladderwinery.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#hook-and-ladder-vineyard

Named for the family's long history as Santa Rosa firefighters, Hook & Ladder produces estate Zinfandel, Pinot Noir, and Chardonnay from organically farmed Russian River Valley fruit, intimate tastings that reflect the family heritage behind every bottle.

### Kendall-Jackson Wine Estate

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa · Top Rated
- Website: https://www.kj.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#kendall-jackson-wine-estate

K-J's Santa Rosa estate headquarters is a revelation for anyone who thinks of it only as a grocery store brand, seated tastings, walking vineyard tours, and estate wines that represent the full depth of Sonoma County's appellations.

### Kunde Winery

- Type: Winery
- Area: Sonoma Valley · Kenwood · 1,850 acres
- Website: https://www.kunde.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#kunde-winery

A fifth-generation family estate with 1,850 acres of vineyards stretching from valley floor to mountain ridge. Cave tours, cave tastings, and one of Sonoma Valley's most impressive estate experiences.

### Lagunitas Brewing Co.

- Type: Brewery
- Address: 1280 N McDowell Blvd, Petaluma
- Website: https://lagunitas.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#lagunitas-brewing-co

Founded in Petaluma in 1993 and now one of the most recognized craft brands nationwide. A massive covered patio hosts live music, and the taproom pours exclusive one-off brews alongside the beloved IPA lineup.

### Larson Family Winery

- Type: Winery
- Area: Sonoma Valley · Carneros
- Website: https://larsonfamilywinery.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#larson-family-winery

A fun, family-friendly estate with a petting zoo, bocce courts, and seriously good Zinfandel and Merlot, the kind of relaxed afternoon winery that earns its place on any Sonoma itinerary.

### Martin Ray Vineyards & Winery

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Laguna Rd, Santa Rosa
- Website: https://www.martinraywinery.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#martin-ray-vineyards-and-winery

A gorgeous estate on Laguna Road in Santa Rosa, panoramic Russian River Valley views, estate Pinot Noir, and a tasting room experience guests describe as one of the most beautiful in Sonoma County. The food, wine, staff, and property all consistently receive five stars.

### Matanzas Creek Winery

- Type: Winery
- Area: Sonoma Valley · Bennett Valley AVA
- Website: https://www.matanzascreek.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#matanzas-creek-winery

Rustic country charm meets refined quality in Bennett Valley, Chardonnay, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc, and Pinot Noir from a stunning estate known for its lavender fields and sweeping valley views.

### Merriam Vineyards

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Healdsburg
- Website: https://www.merriamvineyards.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#merriam-vineyards

A boutique family winery known for elegant, estate-grown Pinot Noir and an elevated tasting experience, intimate, unhurried, and focused on wine that speaks for itself.

### Moonlight Brewing Co.

- Type: Brewery
- Address: 3350 Coffey Ln, Santa Rosa
- Website: https://moonlightbrewing.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#moonlight-brewing-co

A Santa Rosa institution since 1992, small, hands-on, and fiercely independent. Moonlight brews traditional lagers and ales with artisan precision. Death & Taxes and Reality Czeck are among the county's most beloved year-round pours.

### Paradise Ridge Winery

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa
- Website: https://www.paradiseridge.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#paradise-ridge-winery

Hilltop views, sculpture gardens, and estate wines. Paradise Ridge combines art, nature, and Sonoma winemaking in one of the area's most scenically distinctive settings.

### Ridge Winery

- Type: Winery
- Area: Dry Creek Valley · Lytton Springs
- Website: https://www.ridgewine.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#ridge-winery

Old-vine Zinfandel-based blends with the depth and track record that earns a place in serious cellars worldwide. The Lytton Springs estate is Ridge's Dry Creek anchor. Tasting here is a rare experience.

### Russian River Brewing Co.

- Type: Brewery
- Address: 725 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA
- Phone: (707) 545-2337
- Website: https://www.russianriverbrewing.com
- Hours: Daily, pub hours
- Walk from downtown: 6 min
- Map: https://maps.google.com/?cid=505373807435157151
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#russian-river-brewing-co

The brewery that put Sonoma on the global craft beer map. World-famous for Pliny the Elder (double IPA) and the cult annual release of Pliny the Younger (triple IPA, March 20–April 2). Year-round pours include Belgian ales, barrel-aged sours, and California IPAs. Second location with brewery tours in Windsor.

### Russian River Vineyards

- Type: Winery
- Area: Russian River Valley · Forestville
- Website: https://www.russianrivervineyards.com/
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#russian-river-vineyards

A vineyard, brewery, and restaurant rolled into one destination on the Russian River, estate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay alongside farm-fresh food and a laid-back patio that captures the spirit of the appellation.

### Shady Oak Barrel House

- Type: Brewery
- Address: 420 1st St, Santa Rosa, CA
- Phone: (707) 575-7687
- Website: https://shadyoakbarrelhouse.com
- Hours: Taproom hours vary
- Walk from downtown: 6 min
- Map: https://maps.google.com/?cid=4304442913741445784
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#shady-oak-barrel-house

Sonoma County's home for wild ales and barrel-aged sours, complex, tart, and endlessly rotating. A cool casual taproom with the kind of experimental program that draws serious beer travelers from across the state.

### St. Francis Winery

- Type: Winery
- Area: Sonoma Valley · Kenwood
- Website: https://www.stfranciswinery.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#st-francis-winery

Voted best tasting room in the region, award-winning wines paired with chef-crafted bites in a beautiful Sonoma Valley setting. Known for rich reds and a genuinely warm hospitality experience.

### Stonemason Cellars

- Type: Urban Tasting Room
- Area: Urban Tasting Room · Santa Rosa
- Address: 390 Davis St, Santa Rosa, CA

A top-rated boutique tasting room in Santa Rosa consistently praised for its knowledgeable, personable staff and exceptional wines, the kind of intimate, unhurried tasting experience that keeps guests coming back.

### Trecini Winery

- Type: Urban Tasting Room
- Area: Downtown Santa Rosa
- Address: 441 Beaver St, Santa Rosa, CA

A small downtown tasting room on Beaver Street. Open Monday through Thursday only — check ahead before walking over.

### Wilson Artisan Wines

- Type: Winery
- Area: Dry Creek Valley · Healdsburg
- Website: https://www.wilsonartisanwines.com
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#wilson-artisan-wines

Family-owned and focused on old-vine Zinfandel, Petite Sirah, and Rhône varieties from the Dry Creek and Alexander valleys, bold, food-friendly wines with a personal touch.

## Attractions

### Armstrong Redwoods State Reserve

- Type: State Reserve
- Address: Guerneville
- Website: https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=450
- Distance: 35 min drive
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#armstrong-redwoods-state-reserve

Ancient coastal redwoods, some over 1,400 years old and 300 feet tall, tower above quiet forest trails near Guerneville. One of the most accessible old-growth redwood groves in Northern California.

### Bodega Bay

- Type: Coastal
- Address: Sonoma Coast
- Website: https://www.bodegabay.com
- Distance: 50 min drive
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#bodega-bay

The dramatic Sonoma Coast, fresh Dungeness crab, rugged headland hikes, sheltered coves, and the village made famous by Hitchcock's The Birds. The drive alone through the coastal hills is worth the trip.

### Charles M. Schulz Museum

- Type: Museum
- Address: 2301 Hardies Ln, Santa Rosa, CA
- Website: https://schulzmuseum.org
- Hours: Closed Tuesdays
- Distance: 10 min drive
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#charles-m-schulz-museum

Dedicated to the life and work of Santa Rosa's most famous resident, the creator of Peanuts. Original comic strips, biographical exhibits, a recreation of Schulz's studio, and the beloved Snoopy's Home Ice rink next door.

### Hot Air Ballooning

- Type: Adventure
- Address: Various launch sites
- Website: https://www.sonomacounty.com/outdoor-activities/hot-air-ballooning
- Distance: Sonoma County
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#hot-air-ballooning

Drift above the vineyards at sunrise. Sonoma County's ballooning is among the most celebrated in California. Several outfitters launch from Santa Rosa, floating over the Russian River Valley and wine country hills.

### Luther Burbank Center for the Arts

- Type: Performing Arts
- Address: 50 Mark West Springs Rd #500, Santa Rosa, CA
- Website: https://www.lutherburbankcenter.org
- Hours: Event hours vary
- Distance: 5 min drive
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#luther-burbank-center-for-the-arts

The North Bay's premier performing arts center, Broadway tours, world-class music, comedy, dance, and speaker events in a 1,600-seat main hall. Over 50,000 children served annually through its education programs.

### Luther Burbank Home & Gardens

- Type: Historic Site
- Address: 204 Santa Rosa Ave, Santa Rosa, CA
- Website: https://lutherburbank.org
- Hours: Gardens open daily; house tours seasonal
- Walk from downtown: 5 min
- Distance: 5 min walk
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#luther-burbank-home-and-gardens

The meticulously preserved home and experimental gardens of America's celebrated horticulturist, who developed over 800 new plant varieties. Free to visit and a genuinely peaceful downtown stop.

### Museum of Sonoma County

- Type: Museum
- Address: 425 7th St, Santa Rosa, CA
- Website: https://museumsc.org
- Hours: Closed Mondays
- Walk from downtown: 4 min
- Distance: 4 min walk
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#museum-of-sonoma-county

Rotating art exhibitions and historical displays exploring Sonoma County's cultural past and present, and conveniently right around the corner from the downtown hotels.

### Railroad Square Historic District

- Type: Historic District
- Address: Historic 3rd St
- Website: https://www.railroadsquare.net
- Walk from downtown: 10 min
- Distance: 10 min walk
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#railroad-square-historic-district

Built around the restored 1903 Northwestern Pacific Railroad depot, this charming district is lined with antique shops, independent restaurants, and coffee houses, and the starting point for the SMART commuter train.

### Russian River

- Type: River
- Address: Guerneville
- Website: https://www.sonomacounty.com/outdoor-activities/russian-river
- Distance: 30 min drive
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#russian-river

In summer, the Russian River comes alive with canoeing, kayaking, swimming, and fishing. The Guerneville stretch is the most popular. Rent a canoe and float downstream through redwood-lined banks.

### Safari West

- Type: Wildlife
- Address: 3115 Porter Creek Rd, Santa Rosa, CA
- Website: https://www.safariwest.com
- Hours: Tours by reservation
- Distance: 15 min drive
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#safari-west

A 400-acre African wildlife preserve, dubbed the "Sonoma Serengeti", with giraffes, rhinos, zebras, cheetahs, and nearly 900 animals roaming free. Guided jeep tours and glamping tents available.

### Spring Lake Regional Park

- Type: Regional Park
- Address: 393 Violetti Rd, Santa Rosa, CA
- Website: https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/spring-lake-regional-park
- Distance: 15 min drive
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#spring-lake-regional-park

Santa Rosa's 320-acre backyard, a swimming lagoon with lifeguards, boat rentals, hiking trails, and a hands-on natural history center. Popular on warm weekends with locals and visitors alike.

### Trione-Annadel State Park

- Type: State Park
- Address: 6201 Channel Dr, Santa Rosa, CA
- Website: https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=480
- Hours: Sunrise to sunset
- Distance: 15 min drive
- Listing: https://staysantarosa.com/directory#trione-annadel-state-park

Over 5,000 acres of forests, meadows, and streams with 40+ miles of hiking, biking, and equestrian trails right on Santa Rosa's eastern edge. Lake Ilsanjo is a popular fishing and picnic destination in the interior.
